```sql
    `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010`
  WHERE
    gender IN ('male', 'female')
    AND minimum_age IS NULL
    AND maximum_age IS NULL
  GROUP BY
    zipcode
)

-- Step 2: Join with zipcode area and filter by distance
SELECT
  ST_GEOGFROMTEXT(zipcode_geom) AS polygon,
  area_land_meters,
  area_water_meters,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  state_code,
  state_name,
  city,
  county,
  total_population
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area` AS z
  INNER JOIN pop_2010 AS p
    ON z.zipcode = p.zipcode
WHERE
  ST_DWITHIN(
    ST_GEOGFROMTEXT(z.zipcode_geom),
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-122.3321, 47.6062),
    10000
  );
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Find all zip code areas within 10 km of the target coordinates
nearby_zipcodes AS (
  SELECT
    zipcode,
    zipcode_geom,
    area_land_meters,
    area_water_meters,
    latitude,
    longitude,
    state_code,
    state_name,
    city,
    county
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area`
  WHERE ST_DWITHIN(
    ST_GEOGFROMTEXT(zipcode_geom),
    ST_GEOGPOINT(-122.3321, 47.6062),
    10000
  )
),

-- Step 2: Sum male+female population per zipcode (no age constraints)
zip_population AS (
  SELECT
    zipcode,
    SUM(population) AS total_population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010`
  WHERE gender IN ('male', 'female')
    AND minimum_age IS NULL
  GROUP BY zipcode
)

-- Step 3: Join and output all requested columns
SELECT
  ST_GEOGFROMTEXT(n.zipcode_geom) AS polygon,
  n.area_land_meters,
  n.area_water_meters,
  n.latitude,
  n.longitude,
  n.state_code,
  n.state_name,
  n.city,
  n.county,
  COALESCE(zp.total_population, 0) AS total_population
FROM nearby_zipcodes n
LEFT JOIN zip_population zp
  ON n.zipcode = CAST(zp.zipcode AS STRING)
ORDER BY n.zipcode;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH california_tracts AS (
  -- Get all California census tracts with their unique identifiers
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    tract_ce
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_california`
),

income_2015 AS (
  -- Median income data for year 2015 at census tract level
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),

income_2018 AS (
  -- Median income data for year 2018 at census tract level
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE median_income IS NOT NULL
),

combined AS (
  -- Join tracts with both years of income data
  SELECT 
    ct.tract_ce,
    ct.geo_id,
    i15.income_2015,
    i18.income_2018,
    (i18.income_2018 - i15.income_2015) AS income_increase
  FROM california_tracts ct
  INNER JOIN income_2015 i15 ON ct.geo_id = i15.geo_id
  INNER JOIN income_2018 i18 ON ct.geo_id = i18.geo_id
)

-- Get the tract with the largest increase
SELECT 
  tract_ce
FROM combined
ORDER BY income_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get 2015 median income for California tracts
income_2015 AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS median_income_2015
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2015_5yr`
  WHERE LOWER(geo_id) LIKE '06%' -- California state FIPS code is 06
    AND median_income IS NOT NULL
),

-- Get 2018 median income for California tracts
income_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    geo_id,
    median_income AS median_income_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr`
  WHERE LOWER(geo_id) LIKE '06%'
    AND median_income IS NOT NULL
),

-- Join and compute increase
income_change AS (
  SELECT 
    i15.geo_id,
    i15.median_income_2015,
    i18.median_income_2018,
    ROUND(i18.median_income_2018 - i15.median_income_2015, 4) AS income_increase
  FROM income_2015 i15
  INNER JOIN income_2018 i18 ON i15.geo_id = i18.geo_id
)

-- Get the tract code (last part of geo_id, e.g., after the county code)
SELECT 
  SUBSTR(geo_id, -11) AS tract_code
FROM income_change
ORDER BY income_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 24. bq113 (DB: `bls`)
**Question**: Which county in Utah experienced the greatest percentage increase in construction employment from 2000 to 2018, calculated by averaging the employment levels during the third month of each quarter in those years? What is the corresponding percentage increase?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| county_name   |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_2000 |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_2018 |   PERCENTAGE_INCREASE |
|:--------------|------------------------:|------------------------:|----------------------:|
| Utah          |                 10466.2 |                 24692.2 |                135.92 |

**OR**

| COUNTY_NAME   |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_EMPL_2000 |   AVG_CONSTRUCTION_EMPL_2018 |   PERCENTAGE_INCREASE |
|:--------------|-----------------------------:|-----------------------------:|----------------------:|
| Utah County   |                      10466.2 |                      24692.2 |                135.92 |

**OR**

| county            |   pct_increase |
|:------------------|---------------:|
| Utah County, Utah |         135.92 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| county   |   percentage_increase |
|:---------|----------------------:|
| Utah     |               135.923 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| county_name   |   pct_increase |
|:--------------|---------------:|
| Utah          |        135.923 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Query all quarterly BLS QCEW tables for years 2000–2018,
-- extracting construction employment (third month of each quarter) for Utah counties.
WITH construction_data AS (
  SELECT
    geoid,
    -- Extract the year from the table suffix (e.g., '2000_q1' -> 2000)
    CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^(\d{4})') AS INT64) AS year,
    -- Use the construction employment column (prefer NAICS 1012, fallback to SIC 23)
    COALESCE(month3_emplvl_1012_construction, month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS month3_emplvl
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.*`
  WHERE
    -- Filter only to Utah (state FIPS = 49)
    geoid LIKE '49%'
    AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2000_q1' AND '2018_q4'
),

-- Step 2: For each county and year, average the four quarterly third-month values.
avg_per_year AS (
  SELECT
    geoid,
    year,
    AVG(month3_emplvl) AS avg_empl
  FROM construction_data
  WHERE month3_emplvl IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY geoid, year
),

-- Step 3: Isolate the 2000 and 2018 averages per county.
avg_2000 AS (
  SELECT geoid, avg_empl AS avg_2000
  FROM avg_per_year
  WHERE year = 2000
),
avg_2018 AS (
  SELECT geoid, avg_empl AS avg_2018
  FROM avg_per_year
  WHERE year = 2018
),

-- Step 4: Compute the percentage increase for counties that have data in both years.
pct_increase AS (
  SELECT
    a2000.geoid,
    a2000.avg_2000,
    a2018.avg_2018,
    ROUND((a2018.avg_2018 - a2000.avg_2000) / a2000.avg_2000 * 100, 4) AS pct_increase
  FROM avg_2000 a2000
  JOIN avg_2018 a2018
  ON a2000.geoid = a2018.geoid
  WHERE a2000.avg_2000 > 0  -- avoid division by zero
)

-- Step 5: Join with county names and get the highest percentage increase.
SELECT
  c.county_name,
  p.pct_increase
FROM pct_increase p
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties` c
  ON p.geoid = c.county_fips_code
ORDER BY p.pct_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Extract construction employment data for 2000 and 2018 quarters, filtered to Utah counties
qcew_data AS (
  SELECT
    area_fips,
    _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
    month3_emplvl_23_construction
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls_qcew.*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('2000_q1', '2000_q2', '2000_q3', '2000_q4',
                          '2018_q1', '2018_q2', '2018_q3', '2018_q4')
    AND area_fips LIKE '49%'  -- Utah county FIPS codes start with '49'
),

-- Step 2: Average the employment across the 4 quarters for each county per year
yearly_avg AS (
  SELECT
    area_fips,
    CASE
      WHEN table_suffix LIKE '2000_%' THEN 2000
      WHEN table_suffix LIKE '2018_%' THEN 2018
    END AS year,
    AVG(month3_emplvl_23_construction) AS avg_construction_empl
  FROM qcew_data
  GROUP BY area_fips, year
),

-- Step 3: Pair each county's 2000 and 2018 averages side by side
county_comparison AS (
  SELECT
    y2000.area_fips,
    y2000.avg_construction_empl AS avg_2000,
    y2018.avg_construction_empl AS avg_2018
  FROM yearly_avg y2000
  JOIN yearly_avg y2018
    ON y2000.area_fips = y2018.area_fips
  WHERE y2000.year = 2000
    AND y2018.year = 2018
    AND y2000.avg_construction_empl > 0  -- Avoid division by zero
)

-- Step 4 & 5: Join with county names and find the top percentage increase
SELECT
  c.county_name AS county,
  ROUND(((cc.avg_2018 - cc.avg_2000) / cc.avg_2000) * 100, 4) AS percentage_increase
FROM county_comparison cc
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.counties` c
  ON cc.area_fips = c.county_fips_code
WHERE c.state_fips_code = '49'
ORDER BY percentage_increase DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

### 25. bq096 (DB: `gbif`)
**Question**: Determine which year had the earliest date after January on which more than 10 sightings of Sterna paradisaea were recorded north of 40 degrees latitude. For each year, find the first day after January with over 10 sightings of this species in that region, and identify the year whose earliest such date is the earliest among all years.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   year |
|-------:|
|   2023 |

**OR**

|   year |
|-------:|
|   1894 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   year |
|-------:|
|   1894 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   year | first_date_after_jan_over10   |
|-------:|:------------------------------|
|   1894 | 1894-05-23                    |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH daily_sightings AS (
  -- Step 1: Count sightings per day for Sterna paradisaea north of 40°N, after January
  SELECT
    year,
    month,
    day,
    COUNT(*) AS sightings_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
  WHERE species = 'Sterna paradisaea'
    AND decimallatitude > 40
    AND month > 1           -- after January
    AND year IS NOT NULL
    AND month IS NOT NULL
    AND day IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY year, month, day
),
yearly_first_over10 AS (
  -- Step 2: For each year, find the earliest date where sightings > 10
  SELECT
    year,
    MIN(DATE(year, month, day)) AS first_date_after_jan_over10
  FROM daily_sightings
  WHERE sightings_count > 10
  GROUP BY year
)
-- Step 3: Identify the year with the smallest (earliest) such date
SELECT
  year,
  first_date_after_jan_over10
FROM yearly_first_over10
ORDER BY first_date_after_jan_over10 ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH daily_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    month,
    day,
    COUNT(*) AS sighting_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
  WHERE LOWER(species) LIKE '%sterna paradisaea%'
    AND decimallatitude > 40
    AND month > 1
    AND year IS NOT NULL
    AND month IS NOT NULL
    AND day IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY year, month, day
  HAVING sighting_count > 10
),

first_dates_per_year AS (
  SELECT 
    year,
    MIN(DATE(CAST(year AS INT64), CAST(month AS INT64), CAST(day AS INT64))) AS first_date
  FROM daily_counts
  GROUP BY year
)

SELECT year
FROM first_dates_per_year
ORDER BY first_date ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Query to find the most viewed "how" question related to Android development
WITH android_how_questions AS (
    SELECT 
        title,
        view_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
    WHERE 
        -- Title must start with "how" (case-insensitive)
        LOWER(title) LIKE 'how%'
        -- Must be related to Android development (various tag patterns)
        AND (
            LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android%'        -- General Android tag
            OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android-layout%'  -- Android Layout
            OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android-activity%' -- Android Activity
            OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android-intent%'   -- Android Intent
            OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android-fragment%'  -- Android Fragment
            OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android-service%'   -- Android Service
            OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android-widget%'    -- Android Widget
            OR LOWER(tags) LIKE '%android-recyclerview%' -- Android RecyclerView
        )
        -- Only actual questions
        AND post_type_id = 1
)
-- Get the title of the most viewed question
SELECT title
FROM android_how_questions
ORDER BY view_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
    -- Title starts with 'How' (case-insensitive)
    LOWER(title) LIKE 'how%'
    -- Tags contain at least one of the specified patterns (any tag starting with 'android-')
    AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(tags, r'android-')
)
SELECT
  title
FROM
  filtered_questions
ORDER BY
  view_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
-- Compute monthly proportion of Stack Overflow questions tagged with 'python' in 2022
WITH monthly_stats AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM creation_date) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS total_questions,
    COUNTIF(REGEXP_CONTAINS(tags, r'(^|\|)python(\||$)')) AS python_questions
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
  WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2022
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
  month,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(python_questions, total_questions), 4) AS proportion
FROM monthly_stats
ORDER BY month;
```

```sql
SELECT

  ROUND(
    COUNTIF(REGEXP_CONTAINS(tags, r'(^|\|)python(\||$)')) / COUNT(*),
    4
  ) AS proportion
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2022
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month;
```

```sql
-- Query to retrieve titles, artist names, mediums, and original image URLs
-- for objects with 'Photograph' in their name from the 'Photographs' department,
-- with a known artist and an object end date of 1839 or earlier.

SELECT
    o.title,
    o.artist_display_name AS artist_name,
    o.medium,
    i.original_image_url
FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` o
INNER JOIN
    `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` i
    ON o.object_id = i.object_id
WHERE
    -- Filter for objects whose name contains 'Photograph' (case‑insensitive)
    LOWER(o.object_name) LIKE '%photograph%'
    -- Restrict to the 'Photographs' department
    AND o.department = 'Photographs'
    -- End date must be 1839 or earlier
    AND o.object_end_date <= 1839
    -- Exclude objects where the artist is unknown or missing
    AND o.artist_display_name IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(o.artist_display_name) != ''
    AND LOWER(TRIM(o.artist_display_name)) NOT LIKE '%unknown%'
```

```sql
-- Monthly average levels of air pollutants in California for 2020
-- Each pollutant is computed from its daily summary table,
-- filtered to California (state_code = '06') and year 2020.
-- SO2 is scaled by factor 10, Lead by factor 100.
-- Results are monthly averages, rounded to 4 decimal places.

WITH 
pm10_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS pm10
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm10_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_code = '06'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),

pm25_frm_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS pm25_frm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_frm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_code = '06'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),

pm25_nonfrm_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS pm25_nonfrm
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.pm25_nonfrm_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_code = '06'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),

voc_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean), 4) AS voc
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.voc_daily_summary`
  -- Assumption: voc_daily_summary also contains state_code column (common in EPA tables)
  WHERE state_code = '06'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),

so2_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean * 10), 4) AS so2_scaled
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.so2_daily_summary`
  WHERE state_code = '06'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
),

lead_monthly AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date_local) AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(arithmetic_mean * 100), 4) AS lead_scaled
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.lead_daily_summary`
  -- Assumption: lead_daily_summary also contains state_code column (common in EPA tables)
  WHERE state_code = '06'
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date_local) = 2020
  GROUP BY month
)

SELECT
  COALESCE(pm10.month, pm25_frm.month, pm25_nonfrm.month, voc.month, so2.month, lead.month) AS month,
  pm10.pm10,
  pm25_frm.pm25_frm,
  pm25_nonfrm.pm25_nonfrm,
  voc.voc,
  so2.so2_scaled,
  lead.lead_scaled
FROM pm10_monthly AS pm10
FULL OUTER JOIN pm25_frm_monthly AS pm25_frm USING(month)
FULL OUTER JOIN pm25_nonfrm_monthly AS pm25_nonfrm USING(month)
FULL OUTER JOIN voc_monthly AS voc USING(month)
FULL OUTER JOIN so2_monthly AS so2 USING(month)
FULL OUTER JOIN lead_monthly AS lead USING(month)
ORDER BY month;
```

```sql
),

voc_monthly AS (

  WHERE state_name = 'California'

),

so2_monthly AS (

  FROM `bigquery-public-data.epa_historical_air_quality.so2_daily_summary`

),

lead_monthly AS (

)

SELECT
```

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
max_date_cte AS (
    SELECT MAX("date") AS "max_dt"
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES"
),
cutoff_cte AS (
    SELECT
        CASE
            WHEN "max_dt" = LAST_DAY("max_dt") THEN LAST_DAY("max_dt")
            ELSE LAST_DAY(DATEADD('MONTH', -1, "max_dt"))
        END AS "cutoff_date"
    FROM max_date_cte
),
months_cte AS (
    SELECT DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', '2022-01-01'::DATE) AS "month_start"
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATEADD('MONTH', 1, m."month_start")
    FROM months_cte m, cutoff_cte c
    WHERE m."month_start" < c."cutoff_date"
),
total_monthly_volume AS (
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', s."date") AS "month_start",
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS "total_vol_liters"
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    WHERE s."date" >= '2022-01-01'
      AND s."date" <= (SELECT "cutoff_date" FROM cutoff_cte)
    GROUP BY "month_start"
),
category_monthly_volume AS (
    SELECT
        DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', s."date") AS "month_start",
        s."category_name",
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS "vol_liters"
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    WHERE s."date" >= '2022-01-01'
      AND s."date" <= (SELECT "cutoff_date" FROM cutoff_cte)
    GROUP BY "month_start", s."category_name"
),
category_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        cmv."category_name",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cmv."month_start") AS "num_months_with_data",
        AVG(cmv."vol_liters" / tmv."total_vol_liters" * 100) AS "avg_pct_available"
    FROM category_monthly_volume cmv
    JOIN total_monthly_volume tmv ON cmv."month_start" = tmv."month_start"
    GROUP BY cmv."category_name"
),
filtered_categories AS (
    SELECT "category_name"
    FROM category_aggregates
    WHERE "num_months_with_data" >= 24
      AND "avg_pct_available" >= 1.0
),
category_time_series AS (
    SELECT
        m."month_start",
        fc."category_name",
        COALESCE(cmv."vol_liters", 0) / NULLIF(tmv."total_vol_liters", 0) * 100 AS "pct_of_total"
    FROM filtered_categories fc
    CROSS JOIN months_cte m
    JOIN total_monthly_volume tmv ON m."month_start" = tmv."month_start"
    LEFT JOIN category_monthly_volume cmv
        ON m."month_start" = cmv."month_start"
        AND fc."category_name" = cmv."category_name"
),
pairs_correlation AS (
    SELECT
        a."category_name" AS "cat_a",
        b."category_name" AS "cat_b",
        CORR(a."pct_of_total", b."pct_of_total") AS "pearson_r"
    FROM category_time_series a
    JOIN category_time_series b
        ON a."month_start" = b."month_start"
        AND a."category_name" < b."category_name"
    GROUP BY a."category_name", b."category_name"
)
SELECT
    "cat_a" AS liquor_category_1,
    "cat_b" AS liquor_category_2,
    "pearson_r" AS lowest_pearson_correlation
FROM pairs_correlation
WHERE "pearson_r" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "pearson_r" ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Define the date range: from 2022-01-01 to the end of the last fully completed month.
-- The last fully completed month is the month before the current month (no partial current month data).
date_range AS (
    SELECT 
        '2022-01-01'::DATE AS start_date,
        DATE_TRUNC('month', CURRENT_DATE) AS end_of_last_complete_month  -- this is the first day of current month, so all dates < this are in completed months
),
-- Step 2: Compute total monthly sales volume (in liters) for all categories.
monthly_total AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date") AS month_start,
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS total_vol
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    WHERE s."date" >= (SELECT start_date FROM date_range)
      AND s."date" <  (SELECT end_of_last_complete_month FROM date_range)
    GROUP BY month_start
),
-- Step 3: Compute monthly sales volume per category.
monthly_category AS (
    SELECT 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', s."date") AS month_start,
        s."category_name",
        SUM(s."volume_sold_liters") AS cat_vol
    FROM "IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."IOWA_LIQUOR_SALES"."SALES" s
    WHERE s."date" >= (SELECT start_date FROM date_range)
      AND s."date" <  (SELECT end_of_last_complete_month FROM date_range)
    GROUP BY month_start, s."category_name"
    HAVING cat_vol > 0  -- exclude months where the category had no sales (though they won't appear anyway)
),
-- Step 4: Calculate the percentage contribution of each category to the total monthly volume.
category_pct AS (
    SELECT 
        mc.month_start,
        mc."category_name",
        mc.cat_vol / mt.total_vol AS pct
    FROM monthly_category mc
    JOIN monthly_total mt ON mc.month_start = mt.month_start
),
-- Step 5: For each category, compute the average percentage and the number of months with sales (available data).
-- Only keep categories that have at least 24 months of data and an average percentage >= 1%.
category_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        cp."category_name",
        COUNT(DISTINCT cp.month_start) AS num_months,
        AVG(cp.pct) AS avg_pct
    FROM category_pct cp
    GROUP BY cp."category_name"
    HAVING num_months >= 24 AND avg_pct >= 0.01
),
-- Step 6: Get the list of qualifying categories.
qualifying_categories AS (
    SELECT cs."category_name" FROM category_stats cs
),
-- Step 7: Restrict the monthly percentages to only qualifying categories.
qual_pct AS (
    SELECT cp.*
    FROM category_pct cp
    WHERE cp."category_name" IN (SELECT qc."category_name" FROM qualifying_categories qc)
)
-- Step 8: For each unordered pair of qualifying categories, compute the Pearson correlation coefficient
-- of their monthly percentage time series, using only months where both categories have data.
SELECT 
    a."category_name" AS category_1,
    b."category_name" AS category_2,
    CORR(a.pct, b.pct) AS pearson_correlation
FROM qual_pct a
JOIN qual_pct b ON a.month_start = b.month_start
WHERE a."category_name" < b."category_name"  -- ensure each pair only once, and avoid self-joins
GROUP BY a."category_name", b."category_name"
-- Step 9: Order by the smallest (lowest) correlation coefficient.
ORDER BY pearson_correlation ASC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
  SELECT
    name,
    SUM(number) AS total_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'WY' THEN number ELSE 0 END) AS wy_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
  WHERE gender = 'F'

  GROUP BY name
)
```

```sql
    WHERE gender = 'F'
      AND year = 2021
    GROUP BY name
    HAVING wy_count > 0
)

FROM name_aggregates
ORDER BY wy_count / total_count DESC
```

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Get distinct RNA-Seq sample barcodes from the r35 table that have protein_coding gene_type
rna_samples AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        "sample_barcode"
    FROM "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."RNASEQ_HG38_GDC_R35"
    WHERE LOWER("gene_type") = 'protein_coding'
)
-- Step 2: Join with metadata to get project and case info, then filter for TCGA-BRCA
SELECT
    meta."case_barcode" AS "breast_cancer_case_barcode"
FROM "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."PER_SAMPLE_FILE_METADATA_HG38_GDC_R39_V2" meta
JOIN rna_samples rna
    ON meta."sample_barcode" = rna."sample_barcode"
WHERE meta."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
-- Step 3: Group by case and require at least two distinct sample types, one of which is 'Solid Tissue Normal'
GROUP BY meta."case_barcode"
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT meta."sample_type_name") >= 2
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN meta."sample_type_name" = 'Solid Tissue Normal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
ORDER BY meta."case_barcode";
```

```sql
        m."case_barcode",
        m."sample_type_name",

    FROM "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."PER_SAMPLE_FILE_METADATA_HG38_GDC_R39_V2" m
    JOIN "TCGA"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."RNASEQ_HG38_GDC_R35" r
        ON m."sample_barcode" = r."sample_barcode"  -- or appropriate join key
    WHERE m."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND r."gene_type" = 'protein_coding'
),
cases_with_multiple_types AS (
    SELECT "case_barcode"
    FROM rnaseq_genes
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT "sample_type_name") >= 2
       AND SUM(CASE WHEN "sample_type_name" = 'Solid Tissue Normal' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
)
SELECT DISTINCT "case_barcode"
FROM cases_with_multiple_types
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get cytoband coordinates for 15q11 from Mitelman's cytoband table.
WITH cytoband AS (
    SELECT 
        "chromosome",
        "hg38_start",
        "hg38_stop"
    FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."PROD"."CYTOBANDS_HG38"
    WHERE "chromosome" = 'chr15'
      AND "hg38_start" >= 22700000  -- approximate start for 15q11.2
      AND "hg38_stop" <= 28500000   -- approximate end for 15q11.2
),

-- Step 2: Identify case barcodes belonging to the TCGA-LAML study.
-- Use PER_SAMPLE_FILE_METADATA_HG38_GDC_R24 which contains project_short_name.
laml_cases AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "case_barcode"
    FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."PER_SAMPLE_FILE_METADATA_HG38_GDC_R24"
    WHERE "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-LAML'
),

-- Step 3: Get copy number segments on chromosome 15 for those cases.
-- Use COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23 which has absolute copy_number.
segments AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        "start_pos",
        "end_pos",
        "copy_number"
    FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23"
    WHERE "chromosome" = 'chr15'
      AND "case_barcode" IN (SELECT "case_barcode" FROM laml_cases)
),

-- Step 4: Join segments with the cytoband, compute overlap length, and calculate weighted average per case.
overlap_data AS (
    SELECT 
        s."case_barcode",
        s."copy_number",
        -- Overlap length in base pairs (1-based inclusive)
        (LEAST(s."end_pos", c."hg38_stop") - GREATEST(s."start_pos", c."hg38_start") + 1) AS "overlap_length"
    FROM segments s
    CROSS JOIN cytoband c
    WHERE s."start_pos" <= c."hg38_stop"
      AND s."end_pos" >= c."hg38_start"
),

-- Step 5: Aggregate per case: weighted average of copy_number.
weighted_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        ROUND(SUM("copy_number" * "overlap_length") / NULLIF(SUM("overlap_length"), 0), 4) AS "weighted_avg_cn"
    FROM overlap_data
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
)

-- Step 6: Return the case(s) with the highest weighted average copy number.
SELECT 
    "case_barcode",
    "weighted_avg_cn"
FROM weighted_avg
WHERE "weighted_avg_cn" = (SELECT MAX("weighted_avg_cn") FROM weighted_avg)
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH cytoband_15q11 AS (
  -- Get cytoband boundaries for 15q11 (convert 0-based start to 1-based)
  SELECT 
    "chromosome",
    "cytoband_name",
    "hg38_start" + 1 AS "cb_start_1based",  -- UCSC-style 0-based start -> 1-based
    "hg38_stop" AS "cb_end_1based"         -- already 1-based
  FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."PROD"."CYTOBANDS_HG38"
  WHERE "chromosome" = 'chr15'
    AND "cytoband_name" = '15q11'
),
overlap_segments AS (
  -- Join copy number segments with cytoband, compute overlap length
  SELECT 
    seg."case_barcode",
    seg."copy_number",
    -- Compute overlapping interval (1-based inclusive)
    GREATEST(seg."start_pos", cb."cb_start_1based") AS "overlap_start",
    LEAST(seg."end_pos", cb."cb_end_1based") AS "overlap_end",
    -- Overlap length (0 if no overlap)
    GREATEST(LEAST(seg."end_pos", cb."cb_end_1based") - GREATEST(seg."start_pos", cb."cb_start_1based") + 1, 0) AS "overlap_length"
  FROM "TCGA_MITELMAN"."TCGA_VERSIONED"."COPY_NUMBER_SEGMENT_ALLELIC_HG38_GDC_R23" seg
  CROSS JOIN cytoband_15q11 cb
  WHERE seg."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-LAML'
    AND seg."chromosome" = 'chr15'
    AND seg."start_pos" <= cb."cb_end_1based"
    AND seg."end_pos" >= cb."cb_start_1based"
),
case_weighted_avg AS (
  -- Compute weighted average copy number per case
  SELECT 
    "case_barcode",
    SUM("copy_number" * "overlap_length") / NULLIF(SUM("overlap_length"), 0) AS "weighted_avg_cn"
  FROM overlap_segments
  WHERE "overlap_length" > 0
  GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),
ranked AS (
  -- Rank cases by weighted average descending
  SELECT 
    "case_barcode",
    "weighted_avg_cn",
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "weighted_avg_cn" DESC) AS "rnk"
  FROM case_weighted_avg
)
-- Return case(s) with highest weighted average
SELECT "case_barcode"
FROM ranked
WHERE "rnk" = 1
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Final complete SQL query with explanation
-- This query finds female BRCA patients ≤30 years old
-- who have NO problematic annotations (prior treatment issues or redaction)
-- and returns their case barcodes with corresponding GDC file URLs

WITH annotation_patients AS (
  -- Get patients with specific annotation criteria
  SELECT DISTINCT
    case_barcode,
    category AS categoryName,
    classification AS classificationName
  FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Annotations`
  WHERE entity_type = 'Patient'
    AND (category = 'History of unacceptable prior treatment related to a prior/other malignancy'
         OR classification = 'Redaction')
),

clinical_patients AS (
  -- Get target clinical patients: BRCA, female, age ≤ 30
  SELECT DISTINCT
    case_barcode,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS categoryName,
    CAST(NULL AS STRING) AS classificationName
  FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Clinical`
  WHERE disease_code = 'BRCA'
    AND gender = 'FEMALE'
    AND age_at_diagnosis <= 30
),

combined_patients AS (
  -- FULL JOIN, keep only clinical patients not found in annotation set
  SELECT
    COALESCE(a.case_barcode, c.case_barcode) AS case_barcode
  FROM annotation_patients a
  FULL JOIN clinical_patients c
    ON a.case_barcode = c.case_barcode
  WHERE a.categoryName IS NULL
    AND a.classificationName IS NULL
    AND c.case_barcode IS NOT NULL
)

-- Final result: case barcodes with their GDC file URLs
SELECT DISTINCT
  cd.case_barcode,
  url.file_gdc_url
FROM combined_patients cp
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_caseData` cd
  ON cp.case_barcode = cd.case_barcode
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_fileData_current` fd
  ON cd.case_gdc_id = fd.case_gdc_id
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_GDCfileID_to_GCSurl_NEW` url
  ON fd.file_gdc_id = url.file_gdc_id
ORDER BY cd.case_barcode;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH annotations_set AS (
    SELECT 
        case_gdc_id,
        category,
        classification
    FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Annotations`
    WHERE entity_type = 'Patient'
      AND (category = 'History of unacceptable prior treatment related to a prior/other malignancy' 
           OR classification = 'Redaction')
),

clinical_set AS (
    SELECT 
        case_gdc_id,
        case_barcode
    FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Clinical`
    WHERE disease_code = 'BRCA'
      AND gender = 'FEMALE'
      AND age_at_diagnosis IS NOT NULL
      AND age_at_diagnosis <= 30
),

eligible_cases AS (
    SELECT 
        c.case_gdc_id,
        c.case_barcode
    FROM clinical_set c
    FULL JOIN annotations_set a ON c.case_gdc_id = a.case_gdc_id
    WHERE a.category IS NULL 
      AND a.classification IS NULL
)

SELECT DISTINCT
    e.case_barcode,
    u.file_gdc_url AS file_url
FROM eligible_cases e
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_fileData_current` f
    ON e.case_gdc_id = f.case_gdc_id
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_GDCfileID_to_GCSurl_NEW` u
    ON f.file_gdc_id = u.file_gdc_id;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH variant_alleles AS (
    SELECT 
        v."start",
        v."end",
        f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS sample_id,
        (f.value:"genotype"[0]::INTEGER + f.value:"genotype"[1]::INTEGER) AS alt_allele_count,
        2 - alt_allele_count AS ref_allele_count
    FROM 
        "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" v,
        LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v."call") f
    WHERE 
        v."reference_name" = '12'
),

variant_with_pop AS (
    SELECT 
        va."start",
        va."end",
        va.sample_id,
        va.alt_allele_count,
        va.ref_allele_count,
        CASE 
            WHEN si."Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 'case'
            ELSE 'control'
        END AS group_type
    FROM 
        variant_alleles va
    JOIN 
        "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" si
        ON va.sample_id = si."Sample"
),

allele_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        "start",
        "end",
        group_type,
        SUM(alt_allele_count) AS alt_count,
        SUM(ref_allele_count) AS ref_count,
        SUM(alt_allele_count + ref_allele_count) AS total_alleles
    FROM 
        variant_with_pop
    GROUP BY 
        "start", "end", group_type
),

pivot_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        c."start",
        c."end",
        COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN c.group_type = 'case' THEN c.alt_count END), 0) AS case_alt,
        COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN c.group_type = 'case' THEN c.ref_count END), 0) AS case_ref,
        COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN c.group_type = 'control' THEN c.alt_count END), 0) AS control_alt,
        COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN c.group_type = 'control' THEN c.ref_count END), 0) AS control_ref,
        COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN c.group_type = 'case' THEN c.total_alleles END), 0) AS case_total,
        COALESCE(MAX(CASE WHEN c.group_type = 'control' THEN c.total_alleles END), 0) AS control_total
    FROM 
        allele_counts c
    GROUP BY 
        c."start", c."end"
),

chi_squared AS (
    SELECT 
        "start",
        "end",
        case_alt,
        case_ref,
        control_alt,
        control_ref,
        case_total,
        control_total,
        (case_alt + control_alt) AS total_alt,
        (case_ref + control_ref) AS total_ref,
        (case_total + control_total) AS grand_total,
        
        -- Expected counts using floating-point arithmetic (multiply by 1.0)
        (case_total * 1.0 * (case_alt + control_alt) / (case_total + control_total)) AS exp_case_alt,
        (case_total * 1.0 * (case_ref + control_ref) / (case_total + control_total)) AS exp_case_ref,
        (control_total * 1.0 * (case_alt + control_alt) / (case_total + control_total)) AS exp_control_alt,
        (control_total * 1.0 * (case_ref + control_ref) / (case_total + control_total)) AS exp_control_ref
    FROM 
        pivot_counts
    WHERE 
        -- Ensure expected counts are at least 5 (floating comparison)
        (case_total * 1.0 * (case_alt + control_alt) / (case_total + control_total)) >= 5
        AND (case_total * 1.0 * (case_ref + control_ref) / (case_total + control_total)) >= 5
        AND (control_total * 1.0 * (case_alt + control_alt) / (case_total + control_total)) >= 5
        AND (control_total * 1.0 * (case_ref + control_ref) / (case_total + control_total)) >= 5
)

SELECT 
    "start",
    "end",
    ROUND(
        (POWER(GREATEST(ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_alt, 0) +
         POWER(GREATEST(ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_ref, 0) +
         POWER(GREATEST(ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_alt, 0) +
         POWER(GREATEST(ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_ref, 0)),
        4
    ) AS chi_squared_score
FROM 
    chi_squared
WHERE 
    (POWER(GREATEST(ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_alt, 0) +
     POWER(GREATEST(ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_ref, 0) +
     POWER(GREATEST(ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_alt, 0) +
     POWER(GREATEST(ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) - 0.5, 0), 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_ref, 0)) >= 29.71679
ORDER BY 
    chi_squared_score DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Flatten call array to extract per-individual allele counts for variants on chr12
per_variant_ind AS (
  SELECT
    v."start",
    v."end",
    v."reference_name",
    f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS "individual_id",
    (f.value:"genotype"[0]::INT + f.value:"genotype"[1]::INT) AS "alt_allele_count"
  FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" v,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v."call") f
  WHERE v."reference_name" = '12'
),

-- Step 2: Join with sample info to get super population
ind_info AS (
  SELECT
    p."individual_id",
    p."alt_allele_count",
    p."start",
    p."end",
    s."Super_Population"
  FROM per_variant_ind p
  JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" s
    ON p."individual_id" = s."Sample"
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate allele counts for cases (EAS) and controls (all others)
grouped AS (
  SELECT
    "start",
    "end",
    SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN "alt_allele_count" ELSE 0 END) AS "alt_cases",
    SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN "alt_allele_count" ELSE 0 END) AS "alt_controls",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 1 END) * 2 AS "total_cases_alleles",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN 1 END) * 2 AS "total_controls_alleles"
  FROM ind_info
  GROUP BY "start", "end"
)

-- Step 4: Compute chi-squared with Yates correction and filter
SELECT
  "start",
  "end",
  ROUND(
    -- Yates chi-squared = (|ad - bc| - N/2)^2 * N / ( (a+b)(c+d)(a+c)(b+d) )
    (
      POW(
        ABS(
          "alt_cases" * ("total_controls_alleles" - "alt_controls")
          - "alt_controls" * ("total_cases_alleles" - "alt_cases")
        ) - ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") / 2.0,
        2
      ) * ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles")
    ) / (
      ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")
      * (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls"))
      * "total_cases_alleles"
      * "total_controls_alleles"
    ),
    4
  ) AS "chi_squared"
FROM grouped
WHERE
  -- Ensure all expected cell counts are >= 5
  ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls") * "total_cases_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls") * "total_controls_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")) * "total_cases_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")) * "total_controls_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND ROUND(
    (
      POW(
        ABS(
          "alt_cases" * ("total_controls_alleles" - "alt_controls")
          - "alt_controls" * ("total_cases_alleles" - "alt_cases")
        ) - ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") / 2.0,
        2
      ) * ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles")
    ) / (
      ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")
      * (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls"))
      * "total_cases_alleles"
      * "total_controls_alleles"
    ),
    4
  ) >= 29.71679
ORDER BY "chi_squared" DESC;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH active_stations AS (
    -- Select only stations with status 'active'
    SELECT "station_id"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATIONS"
    WHERE "status" = 'active'
),
station_trips AS (
    -- Aggregate trips per active station
    SELECT
        t."start_station_id",
        COUNT(*) AS total_trips,
        ROUND(AVG(t."duration_minutes"), 4) AS avg_duration_minutes
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
    INNER JOIN active_stations s
        ON t."start_station_id" = s."station_id"
    GROUP BY t."start_station_id"
),
overall_total AS (
    -- Total starting trips from all active stations
    SELECT SUM(total_trips) AS overall_trips
    FROM station_trips
),
ranked_stations AS (
    -- Compute rank (dense rank) and percentage
    SELECT
        st."start_station_id",
        st.total_trips,
        st.avg_duration_minutes,
        ROUND(st.total_trips * 100.0 / ot.overall_trips, 4) AS percentage,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY st.total_trips DESC) AS rnk
    FROM station_trips st
    CROSS JOIN overall_total ot
)
-- Final output: top 15 stations ordered by rank
SELECT
    "start_station_id" AS station_id,
    total_trips,
    percentage,
    avg_duration_minutes
FROM ranked_stations
WHERE rnk <= 15
ORDER BY rnk;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Join active stations with their starting trips
active_station_trips AS (
    SELECT 
        s."station_id",
        t."duration_minutes"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATIONS" s
    INNER JOIN "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
        ON s."station_id" = t."start_station_id"
    WHERE LOWER(s."status") = 'active'
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate per station: total trips and avg duration
station_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_trips",
        ROUND(AVG("duration_minutes"), 4) AS "avg_duration_minutes"
    FROM active_station_trips
    GROUP BY "station_id"
),

-- Step 3: Compute the grand total of trips from all active stations
overall_total AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "grand_total"
    FROM station_stats
),

-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips (DENSE_RANK includes ties)
ranked_stations AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        "total_trips",
        "avg_duration_minutes",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM station_stats
)

-- Step 5: Final selection of top 15 stations (including ties)
SELECT 
    "station_id",
    "total_trips",
    ROUND("total_trips" * 100.0 / (SELECT "grand_total" FROM overall_total), 4) AS "percentage",
    "avg_duration_minutes"
FROM ranked_stations
WHERE "rank" <= 15
ORDER BY "rank";
```
</details>

```sql
-- Breakdown of total articles per category and percentage mentioning "education"
SELECT
  category,
  COUNT(*) AS total_articles,
  COUNTIF(LOWER(title) LIKE '%education%' OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%') AS education_mention_count,
  ROUND(
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      COUNTIF(LOWER(title) LIKE '%education%' OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%'),
      COUNT(*)
    ) * 100,
    4
  ) AS education_percentage
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
GROUP BY
  category
ORDER BY
  category;
```

```sql
WITH category_stats AS (

    COUNT(*) AS total_articles,
    COUNTIF(LOWER(title) LIKE '%education%' OR LOWER(body) LIKE '%education%') AS education_articles
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext` TABLESAMPLE SYSTEM (1 PERCENT)
  GROUP BY category
)
SELECT
  category,
  total_articles,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(education_articles, total_articles) * 100, 4) AS education_percentage
FROM category_stats
```

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH corn_production AS (
  -- Aggregate corn production in bushels for each state in 2022
  SELECT
    state_name,
    SUM(value) AS corn_total
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
  WHERE
    year = 2022
    AND commodity_desc = 'CORN'
    AND group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND unit_desc = 'BU'
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY state_name
),

mushroom_production AS (
  -- Aggregate mushroom production (any unit) for each state in 2022
  SELECT
    state_name,
    SUM(value) AS mushroom_total
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
  WHERE
    year = 2022
    AND commodity_desc = 'MUSHROOMS'
    AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY state_name
)

-- Combine both results using a full outer join to show all states that have either corn or mushroom data
SELECT
  COALESCE(c.state_name, m.state_name) AS state_name,
  COALESCE(c.corn_total, 0) AS corn_production,
  COALESCE(m.mushroom_total, 0) AS mushroom_production
FROM corn_production c
FULL OUTER JOIN mushroom_production m
  ON c.state_name = m.state_name
ORDER BY state_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH corn_data AS (
  -- Aggregate 2022 corn production from FIELD CROPS, measured in bushels (BU)
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    ROUND(SUM(value), 4) AS corn_production
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
  WHERE year = 2022
    AND LOWER(commodity_desc) = 'corn'
    AND group_desc = 'FIELD CROPS'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND unit_desc = 'BU'
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY state_name
),
mushroom_data AS (
  -- Aggregate 2022 mushroom production from HORTICULTURE
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    ROUND(SUM(value), 4) AS mushroom_production
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.crops`
  WHERE year = 2022
    AND LOWER(commodity_desc) = 'mushrooms'
    AND group_desc = 'HORTICULTURE'
    AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
    AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
    AND value IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY state_name
)
-- FULL OUTER JOIN preserves all states from both datasets
SELECT 
  COALESCE(c.state_name, m.state_name) AS state_name,
  c.corn_production,
  m.mushroom_production
FROM corn_data c
FULL OUTER JOIN mushroom_data m
  ON c.state_name = m.state_name
ORDER BY state_name;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH general_forum AS (
    SELECT "Id"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
    WHERE LOWER("Title") = 'general'
    FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY
),

sub_forums AS (
    SELECT "Id",
           "Title"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
    WHERE "ParentForumId" = (SELECT "Id" FROM general_forum)
),

topic_data AS (
    SELECT
        t."Id"                                          AS topic_id,
        t."CreationDate",
        t."Title"                                       AS topic_title,
        t."TotalViews",
        sf."Title"                                      AS sub_forum_title,
        m."Id"                                          AS message_id,
        m."PostUserId",
        v."Id"                                          AS vote_id
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMTOPICS t
    JOIN sub_forums sf ON t."ForumId" = sf."Id"
    LEFT JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES m ON t."Id" = m."ForumTopicId"
    LEFT JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGEVOTES v ON m."Id" = v."ForumMessageId"
),

aggregated AS (
    SELECT
        topic_id,
        "CreationDate",
        topic_title,
        COALESCE("TotalViews", 0)       AS total_views,
        COUNT(DISTINCT message_id)      AS reply_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT "PostUserId")    AS distinct_user_replies_count,
        COUNT(DISTINCT vote_id)         AS total_upvotes
    FROM topic_data
    GROUP BY topic_id, "CreationDate", topic_title, total_views
)

SELECT
    TO_TIMESTAMP("CreationDate" / 1000000)              AS creation_date,
    topic_title                                          AS title,
    'General'                                            AS parent_forum_title,
    COALESCE(reply_count, 0)                             AS reply_count,
    COALESCE(distinct_user_replies_count, 0)             AS distinct_user_replies_count,
    COALESCE(total_upvotes, 0)                           AS total_upvotes,
    total_views
FROM aggregated
ORDER BY "CreationDate" ASC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    "general_forum" AS (
        -- Step 1: Find the Id of the parent forum titled 'General'
        SELECT "Id"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
        WHERE "Title" = 'General'
    ),
    "sub_forums" AS (
        -- Step 2: Find all sub-forums under 'General' (where ParentForumId matches any General Id)
        SELECT "Id"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
        WHERE "ParentForumId" IN (SELECT "Id" FROM "general_forum")
    ),
    "topic_base" AS (
        -- Step 3: Get all topics that belong to any sub-forum under General
        SELECT
            ft."Id" AS "topic_id",
            ft."CreationDate",
            ft."Title" AS "topic_title",
            ft."TotalViews",
            ft."ForumId"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMTOPICS ft
        WHERE ft."ForumId" IN (SELECT "Id" FROM "sub_forums")
    ),
    "message_aggregates" AS (
        -- Step 4 & 5: Count total messages (reply count) and distinct users per topic
        SELECT
            fm."ForumTopicId",
            COUNT(fm."Id") AS "reply_count",
            COUNT(DISTINCT fm."PostUserId") AS "distinct_user_replies_count"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES fm
        WHERE fm."ForumTopicId" IN (SELECT "topic_id" FROM "topic_base")
        GROUP BY fm."ForumTopicId"
    ),
    "upvote_aggregates" AS (
        -- Step 6: Count total upvotes on all messages within each topic
        SELECT
            fm."ForumTopicId",
            COUNT(fmv."Id") AS "total_upvotes"
        FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES fm
        LEFT JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGEVOTES fmv
            ON fm."Id" = fmv."ForumMessageId"
        WHERE fm."ForumTopicId" IN (SELECT "topic_id" FROM "topic_base")
        GROUP BY fm."ForumTopicId"
    )
-- Step 7: Assemble final output with earliest 5 topics
SELECT
    TO_TIMESTAMP(tb."CreationDate" / 1000000) AS "CreationDate",
    tb."topic_title" AS "Title",
    f."Title" AS "ParentForumTitle",
    COALESCE(ma."reply_count", 0) AS "ReplyCount",
    COALESCE(ma."distinct_user_replies_count", 0) AS "DistinctUserRepliesCount",
    COALESCE(ua."total_upvotes", 0) AS "TotalUpvotes",
    tb."TotalViews"
FROM "topic_base" tb
LEFT JOIN "message_aggregates" ma
    ON tb."topic_id" = ma."ForumTopicId"
LEFT JOIN "upvote_aggregates" ua
    ON tb."topic_id" = ua."ForumTopicId"
JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS f
    ON tb."ForumId" = f."Id"
ORDER BY tb."CreationDate" ASC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

### 42. bq402 (DB: `ecommerce`)
**Question**: Calculate the conversion rate from unique visitors to purchasers by using data exclusively from the `web_analytics` table in the `data-to-insights.ecommerce` dataset. A visitor is defined as a unique `fullVisitorId` present in the table, while a purchaser is a visitor who has at least one transaction recorded (`totals.transactions` is not null). The conversion rate is computed by dividing the number of unique purchasers by the total number of unique visitors. Additionally, calculate the average number of transactions per purchaser, considering only those visitors who have made at least one transaction.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|         0.0269845 |                          1.24412 |

**OR**

|   TOTAL_UNIQUE_VISITORS |   UNIQUE_PURCHASERS |   TOTAL_TRANSACTIONS |   CONVERSION_RATE_PERCENTAGE |   AVG_TRANSACTIONS_PER_PURCHASER |
|------------------------:|--------------------:|---------------------:|-----------------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|                  741721 |               20015 |                24901 |                          2.7 |                             1.24 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   unique_visitors |   unique_purchasers |   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|--------------------:|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|            741721 |               20015 |             0.027 |                           1.2441 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   conversion_rate |   avg_transactions_per_purchaser |
|------------------:|---------------------------------:|
|             0.027 |                           1.2441 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  visitors AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT fullVisitorId
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
  ),
  purchasers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT fullVisitorId
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
    WHERE totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
  ),
  purchaser_transactions AS (
    SELECT
      fullVisitorId,
      SUM(totals.transactions) AS total_transactions
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
    WHERE totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY fullVisitorId
  )
SELECT
  ROUND(
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM purchasers),
      (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM visitors)
    ),
    4
  ) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(
    (SELECT AVG(total_transactions) FROM purchaser_transactions),
    4
  ) AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Total unique visitors across all sessions
  visitor_stats AS (
    SELECT
      COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId) AS total_visitors
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
  ),

  -- Purchasers: visitors with at least one transaction,
  -- along with their total transaction count across all sessions
  purchaser_stats AS (
    SELECT
      fullVisitorId,
      SUM(totals.transactions) AS total_transactions_per_visitor
    FROM `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
    WHERE totals.transactions IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY fullVisitorId
  ),

  -- Aggregate purchaser-level data
  aggregated AS (
    SELECT
      (SELECT total_visitors FROM visitor_stats) AS unique_visitors,
      COUNT(DISTINCT fullVisitorId)                AS unique_purchasers,
      AVG(total_transactions_per_visitor)          AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
    FROM purchaser_stats
  )

-- Final output: conversion rate and average transactions per purchaser
SELECT
  unique_visitors,
  unique_purchasers,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(unique_purchasers, unique_visitors), 4) AS conversion_rate,
  ROUND(avg_transactions_per_purchaser, 4)                  AS avg_transactions_per_purchaser
FROM aggregated;
```
</details>

```sql
-- CTE to generate all ages from 12 to 18
WITH ages AS (
    SELECT 12 AS "age" UNION ALL
    SELECT 13 UNION ALL
    SELECT 14 UNION ALL
    SELECT 15 UNION ALL
    SELECT 16 UNION ALL
    SELECT 17 UNION ALL
    SELECT 18
),

-- Base death records with age and race information for ages 12-18 (years)
base_deaths AS (
    SELECT
        d."Id",
        d."Age",
        CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS "is_black"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.DEATHRECORDS d
    LEFT JOIN DEATH.DEATH.RACE r ON d."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE d."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
      AND d."AgeType" = 1   -- assuming 1 = years
),

-- Distinct death record IDs associated with ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'vehicle'
vehicle_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT e."DeathRecordId"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS e
    JOIN DEATH.DEATH.ICD10CODE i ON e."Icd10Code" = i."Code"
    WHERE LOWER(i."Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
),

-- Distinct death record IDs associated with ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'firearm'
firearm_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT e."DeathRecordId"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS e
    JOIN DEATH.DEATH.ICD10CODE i ON e."Icd10Code" = i."Code"
    WHERE LOWER(i."Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
),

-- Aggregate counts for vehicle-related deaths per age
vehicle_agg AS (
    SELECT
        b."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT b."Id") AS "vehicle_total",
        SUM(b."is_black")      AS "vehicle_black"
    FROM base_deaths b
    JOIN vehicle_death_ids v ON b."Id" = v."DeathRecordId"
    GROUP BY b."Age"
),

-- Aggregate counts for firearm-related deaths per age
firearm_agg AS (
    SELECT
        b."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT b."Id") AS "firearm_total",
        SUM(b."is_black")      AS "firearm_black"
    FROM base_deaths b
    JOIN firearm_death_ids f ON b."Id" = f."DeathRecordId"
    GROUP BY b."Age"
)

-- Final output: every age from 12-18 with vehicle and firearm counts (coalesce 0 for missing)
SELECT
    a."age",
    COALESCE(v."vehicle_total", 0) AS "vehicle_total",
    COALESCE(v."vehicle_black", 0) AS "vehicle_black",
    COALESCE(f."firearm_total", 0) AS "firearm_total",
    COALESCE(f."firearm_black", 0) AS "firearm_black"
FROM ages a
LEFT JOIN vehicle_agg v ON a."age" = v."Age"
LEFT JOIN firearm_agg f ON a."age" = f."Age"
ORDER BY a."age";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH vehicle_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
),
firearm_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
),
vehicle_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS" eac
    INNER JOIN vehicle_icd_codes vic ON eac."Icd10Code" = vic."Code"
),
firearm_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS" eac
    INNER JOIN firearm_icd_codes fic ON eac."Icd10Code" = fic."Code"
),
vehicle_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" dr
    INNER JOIN vehicle_death_ids vdi ON dr."Id" = vdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE" r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
),
firearm_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" dr
    INNER JOIN firearm_death_ids fdi ON dr."Id" = fdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE" r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
)
SELECT
    "Age",
    'vehicle' AS cause,
    total_deaths,
    black_deaths
FROM vehicle_stats
UNION ALL
SELECT
    "Age",
    'firearm' AS cause,
    total_deaths,
    black_deaths
FROM firearm_stats
ORDER BY "Age", cause;
```

### 44. local018 (DB: `California_Traffic_Collision`)
**Question**: For the primary collision factor violation category that was the most common cause of traffic accidents in 2021, how many percentage points did its share of annual road incidents in 2021 decrease compared to its share in 2011?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   MAX(CASE WHEN COLLISION_YEAR = 2011 THEN PERCENTAGE_SHARE END) - MAX(CASE WHEN COLLISION_YEAR = 2021 THEN PERCENTAGE_SHARE END) |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------:|
|                                                                                                                         -0.553654 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   percentage_point_decrease |
|----------------------------:|
|                     -0.5537 |

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|   percentage_points_decrease |
|-----------------------------:|
|                      -0.5537 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total collisions in 2021 and 2011
WITH
total_2021 AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS "total_2021"
    FROM "collisions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") = '2021'
),
total_2011 AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS "total_2011"
    FROM "collisions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") = '2011'
),
-- Step 2: Find the most common pcf_violation_category in 2021
top_category_2021 AS (
    SELECT "pcf_violation_category"
    FROM "collisions"
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") = '2021'
    GROUP BY "pcf_violation_category"
    ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Step 3: Count incidents for that category in both years
category_counts AS (
    SELECT
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "collisions"
         WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") = '2021'
           AND "pcf_violation_category" = (SELECT "pcf_violation_category" FROM top_category_2021)
        ) AS "cnt_2021",
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "collisions"
         WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") = '2011'
           AND "pcf_violation_category" = (SELECT "pcf_violation_category" FROM top_category_2021)
        ) AS "cnt_2011"
)
-- Step 4: Compute shares and percentage-point decrease
SELECT
    ROUND(
        (SELECT "cnt_2011" FROM category_counts) * 100.0 / (SELECT "total_2011" FROM total_2011)
        -
        (SELECT "cnt_2021" FROM category_counts) * 100.0 / (SELECT "total_2021" FROM total_2021),
        4
    ) AS "percentage_points_decrease"
FROM top_category_2021;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Total accidents in each year
total_by_year AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "collision_date") AS "year",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_count"
    FROM collisions
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") IN ('2011', '2021')
    GROUP BY strftime('%Y', "collision_date")
),
-- Accidents per PCF violation category per year
category_by_year AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "collision_date") AS "year",
        "pcf_violation_category",
        COUNT(*) AS "category_count"
    FROM collisions
    WHERE strftime('%Y', "collision_date") IN ('2011', '2021')
    GROUP BY strftime('%Y', "collision_date"), "pcf_violation_category"
),
-- The most common violation category in 2021
top_category_2021 AS (
    SELECT "pcf_violation_category"
    FROM category_by_year
    WHERE "year" = '2021'
    ORDER BY "category_count" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Share percentages for that category in both years
shares AS (
    SELECT 
        c."year",
        c."category_count" * 100.0 / t."total_count" AS "share"
    FROM category_by_year c
    JOIN total_by_year t ON c."year" = t."year"
    WHERE c."pcf_violation_category" = (SELECT "pcf_violation_category" FROM top_category_2021)
)
-- Calculate percentage point decrease: share_2011 - share_2021
SELECT 
    ROUND(
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = '2011' THEN "share" ELSE 0 END) - 
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = '2021' THEN "share" ELSE 0 END),
        4
    ) AS "percentage_point_decrease"
FROM shares;
```
</details>

### 45. local019 (DB: `WWE`)
**Question**: For the NXT title that had the shortest match (excluding titles with "title change"), what were the names of the two wrestlers involved?

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

|:--------------|:-------------|
| Bron Breakker | Duke Hudson  |

</details>

<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

|:--------------|:------------|
| Bron Breakker | Duke Hudson |

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Filter matches for NXT titles without title changes, and with valid duration
valid_matches AS (
    SELECT 
        m.id AS match_id,
        m.winner_id,
        m.loser_id,
        m.duration,
        b.name AS belt_name
    FROM "Matches" AS m
    JOIN "Belts" AS b ON m.title_id = b.id
    WHERE 
        b.name LIKE '%NXT%'
        AND m.title_change = 0
        AND m.duration IS NOT NULL 
        AND m.duration != ''
),
-- Parse duration from 'MM:SS' format to total seconds
match_with_seconds AS (
    SELECT 
        *,
        CAST(SUBSTR(duration, 1, INSTR(duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 
        + CAST(SUBSTR(duration, INSTR(duration, ':') + 1) AS INTEGER) AS duration_sec
    FROM valid_matches
),
-- Select the shortest match
shortest_match AS (
    SELECT * 
    FROM match_with_seconds
    ORDER BY duration_sec ASC
    LIMIT 1
)
-- Get the names of the two wrestlers involved
SELECT 
    w1.name AS wrestler1,
    w2.name AS wrestler2
FROM shortest_match AS sm
JOIN "Wrestlers" AS w1 ON sm.winner_id = w1.id
JOIN "Wrestlers" AS w2 ON sm.loser_id = w2.id;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the NXT promotion ID
WITH nxt_promotion AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM Promotions
    WHERE name = 'NXT'
),

-- Step 2: Find all card IDs belonging to NXT shows
nxt_cards AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM Cards
    WHERE promotion_id IN (SELECT id FROM nxt_promotion)
),

-- Step 3: Get all NXT title matches (excluding title changes) with parsed durations
nxt_title_matches AS (
    SELECT 
        m.id AS match_id,
        m.winner_id,
        m.loser_id,
        b.name AS title_name,
        -- Convert duration from 'MM:SS' format to total seconds
        CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + 
        CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 4, 2) AS INTEGER) AS duration_seconds
    FROM Matches m
    INNER JOIN Cards c ON m.card_id = c.id
    INNER JOIN Belts b ON m.title_id = b.id
    WHERE c.id IN (SELECT id FROM nxt_cards)
      AND m.title_change = 0          -- Exclude matches where title changed hands
      AND m.duration != ''             -- Only consider matches with recorded duration
      AND b.name LIKE '%NXT%'         -- Only consider NXT-branded titles
),

-- Step 4: Identify the match with the shortest duration
shortest_match AS (
    SELECT 
        winner_id,
        loser_id
    FROM nxt_title_matches
    ORDER BY duration_seconds ASC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 5: Retrieve the names of the two wrestlers involved
SELECT 
    w_winner.name AS winner_name,
    w_loser.name AS loser_name
FROM shortest_match sm
INNER JOIN Wrestlers w_winner ON CAST(sm.winner_id AS INTEGER) = w_winner.id
INNER JOIN Wrestlers w_loser ON CAST(sm.loser_id AS INTEGER) = w_loser.id;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute annual delivered order volumes for 2016, 2017, 2018
WITH annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS "year",
        COUNT(*) AS "annual_count"
    FROM "olist_orders"
    WHERE 
        "order_status" = 'delivered'
        AND "order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
        AND strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") IN ('2016', '2017', '2018')
    GROUP BY "year"
),

-- Step 2: Identify the year with the lowest annual volume
target_year AS (
    SELECT "year"
    FROM "annual_volumes"
    ORDER BY "annual_count" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 3: Compute monthly delivered order volumes for that specific year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        strftime('%m', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS "month",
        COUNT(*) AS "monthly_count"
    FROM "olist_orders"
    WHERE 
        "order_status" = 'delivered'
        AND "order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
        AND strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") = (SELECT "year" FROM "target_year")
    GROUP BY "month"
)

-- Step 4: Return the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX("monthly_count") AS "highest_monthly_volume"
FROM "monthly_volumes";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Extract year and month for delivered orders in 2016-2018
delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 1, 4) AS year,
        SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 6, 2) AS month
    FROM olist_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
      AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
      AND SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 1, 4) IN ('2016', '2017', '2018')
),
-- Count annual delivered orders volume
annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        COUNT(*) AS annual_count
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY year
),
-- Identify the year with the lowest annual volume
lowest_volume_year AS (
    SELECT year
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY annual_count ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Count monthly delivered orders for that specific year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        month,
        COUNT(*) AS monthly_count
    FROM delivered_orders
    WHERE year = (SELECT year FROM lowest_volume_year)
    GROUP BY year, month
)
-- Return the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX(monthly_count) AS highest_monthly_delivered_orders_volume
FROM monthly_volumes;
```

### 47. local038 (DB: `Pagila`)
**Question**: Could you help me determine which actor starred most frequently in English-language children's category films that were rated either G or PG, had a running time of 120 minutes or less, and were released between 2000 and 2010? Please provide the actor's full name.

**Status**: Baseline ✅ | SlayQL ✅

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| actor_full_name   |
|:------------------|
| HELEN VOIGHT      |

**OR**

| first_name   | last_name   |   FILM_COUNT |
|:-------------|:------------|-------------:|
| HELEN        | VOIGHT      |            3 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| actor_full_name   |
|:------------------|
| HELEN VOIGHT      |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (✅)</b></summary>

| actor_full_name   |
|:------------------|
| HELEN VOIGHT      |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Understand the question
-- Find the actor who appeared most often in films that meet ALL these criteria:
--   - English language (language_id = 1 based on sample data)
--   - Category is 'Children'
--   - Rating is 'G' or 'PG'
--   - Running time (length) <= 120 minutes
--   - Release year between 2000 and 2010 (inclusive)
-- Return the actor's full name (first_name + last_name)

-- Step 2: Identify relevant tables
-- film: film_id, language_id, length, rating, release_year
-- film_category: film_id, category_id
-- category: category_id, name (we need 'Children')
-- film_actor: actor_id, film_id
-- actor: actor_id, first_name, last_name

-- Step 3: Design query with CTEs for clarity

WITH 
-- Filter films that meet all criteria
qualifying_films AS (
    SELECT 
        f.film_id
    FROM film f
    JOIN film_category fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
    WHERE 
        f.language_id = 1                                -- English language
        AND LOWER(c.name) = 'children'                   -- Children's category
        AND (f.rating = 'G' OR f.rating = 'PG')         -- Rating G or PG
        AND f.length <= 120                              -- Running time <= 120 minutes
        AND CAST(f.release_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010  -- Release year range
),

-- Count appearances per actor in qualifying films
actor_film_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        fa.actor_id,
        COUNT(DISTINCT fa.film_id) AS film_count
    FROM film_actor fa
    INNER JOIN qualifying_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
    GROUP BY fa.actor_id
),

-- Get the maximum count
max_count AS (
    SELECT MAX(film_count) AS max_film_count
    FROM actor_film_counts
)

-- Select the actor(s) with the highest count, with full name
SELECT 
    a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM actor a
INNER JOIN actor_film_counts afc ON a.actor_id = afc.actor_id
CROSS JOIN max_count mc
WHERE afc.film_count = mc.max_film_count
ORDER BY actor_full_name;

-- Note: If there are ties for the most frequent actor, this returns all of them.
-- The question asks for "which actor", implying one, but ties are possible so we return all.
-- The ORDER BY is for consistent output.
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (✅)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
    -- Identify the English language ID from the language lookup table
    english_language AS (
        SELECT language_id 
        FROM language 
        WHERE name = 'English'
    ),
    -- Films satisfying: English language, G or PG rating, ≤120 minutes, released 2000-2010
    base_films AS (
        SELECT f.film_id
        FROM film f
        CROSS JOIN english_language el
        WHERE f.language_id = el.language_id
          AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')
          AND f.length <= 120
          AND CAST(f.release_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
    ),
    -- Films belonging to the 'Children' category
    children_films AS (
        SELECT fc.film_id
        FROM film_category fc
        JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
        WHERE c.name = 'Children'
    ),
    -- Intersection: English-language children's films meeting all criteria
    qualified_films AS (
        SELECT bf.film_id
        FROM base_films bf
        INNER JOIN children_films cf ON bf.film_id = cf.film_id
    ),
    -- Count how many qualified films each actor appeared in
    actor_appearances AS (
        SELECT fa.actor_id, COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
        FROM film_actor fa
        INNER JOIN qualified_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
        GROUP BY fa.actor_id
    ),
    -- Select the actor with the highest appearance count
    top_actor AS (
        SELECT actor_id
        FROM actor_appearances
        ORDER BY appearance_count DESC
        LIMIT 1
    )
-- Return the full name of the top actor
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM actor a
INNER JOIN top_actor ta ON a.actor_id = ta.actor_id;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Get all unicorn companies with industry and year
WITH unicorn_companies AS (
    SELECT
        cf."company_id",
        cd."date_joined",
        ci."industry"
    FROM "companies_funding" cf
    JOIN "companies_dates" cd ON cf."company_id" = cd."company_id"
    JOIN "companies_industries" ci ON cf."company_id" = ci."company_id"
    WHERE cf."valuation" >= 1000000000
      AND CAST(strftime('%Y', cd."date_joined") AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2019 AND 2021
),

-- Step 2: Count unicorn companies per industry per year
industry_yearly_counts AS (
    SELECT
        "industry",
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "date_joined") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        COUNT(*) AS "num_unicorns"
    FROM unicorn_companies
    GROUP BY "industry", "year"
),

-- Step 3: Find the top industry (highest total unicorn count across all years 2019-2021)
top_industry AS (
    SELECT
        "industry",
        SUM("num_unicorns") AS "total_unicorns"
    FROM industry_yearly_counts
    GROUP BY "industry"
    ORDER BY "total_unicorns" DESC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 4: Calculate average number of new unicorn companies per year in top industry
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG("num_unicorns"), 4) AS "average_new_unicorns_per_year"
FROM industry_yearly_counts
WHERE "industry" = (SELECT "industry" FROM top_industry);
```

```sql
    GROUP BY ci.industry, SUBSTR(cd.date_joined, 1, 4)
),
industry_total AS (
    SELECT 
        industry,
        SUM(cnt) AS total_unicorns,
        COUNT(DISTINCT year) AS num_years
    FROM unicorn_yearly
    GROUP BY industry
),
top_industry AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM industry_total
    ORDER BY total_unicorns DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(cnt), 4) AS avg_new_unicorns_per_year
FROM unicorn_yearly
WHERE industry IN (SELECT industry FROM top_industry);
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the best-selling artist (artist with highest total sales)
WITH artist_sales AS (
    SELECT 
        ar."ArtistId",
        ar."Name",
        ROUND(SUM(ii."UnitPrice" * ii."Quantity"), 4) AS total_sales
    FROM "artists" ar
    JOIN "albums" al ON ar."ArtistId" = al."ArtistId"
    JOIN "tracks" t ON al."AlbumId" = t."AlbumId"

    ORDER BY total_sales DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1

    FROM "albums" al
    JOIN best_artist ba ON al."ArtistId" = ba."ArtistId"
),
-- Step 3: Calculate total spent per customer on these albums
customer_spending AS (
    SELECT 
        c."CustomerId",
        c."FirstName",
        ROUND(SUM(ii."UnitPrice" * ii."Quantity"), 4) AS total_spent
    FROM "customers" c
    JOIN "invoices" i ON c."CustomerId" = i."CustomerId"
    JOIN "invoice_items" ii ON i."InvoiceId" = ii."InvoiceId"
    JOIN "tracks" t ON ii."TrackId" = t."TrackId"
    JOIN best_artist_albums baa ON t."AlbumId" = baa."AlbumId"
    GROUP BY c."CustomerId"
)
-- Step 4: Filter customers who spent less than $1
SELECT 
    "FirstName",
    total_spent AS amount_spent
FROM customer_spending
WHERE total_spent < 1.00
ORDER BY total_spent DESC NULLS LAST;
```
