```sql
WITH trip_data AS (
    -- Extract year-month from start_date and convert duration_sec to minutes
    SELECT 
        FORMAT_DATE('%Y%m', DATE(start_date)) AS year_month,
        start_date,
        ROUND(duration_sec / 60, 4) AS duration_minutes
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
),
ranked_trips AS (
    -- Assign chronological ranks within each year-month group
    SELECT 
        year_month,
        duration_minutes,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year_month ORDER BY start_date ASC) AS rn_asc,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year_month ORDER BY start_date DESC) AS rn_desc
    FROM trip_data
)
SELECT 
    year_month,
    -- First trip: the one with earliest start_date in the group
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn_asc = 1 THEN duration_minutes END) AS first_trip_duration_minutes,
    -- Last trip: the one with latest start_date in the group
    MAX(CASE WHEN rn_desc = 1 THEN duration_minutes END) AS last_trip_duration_minutes,
    -- Highest trip duration in the group
    MAX(duration_minutes) AS highest_trip_duration_minutes,
    -- Lowest trip duration in the group
    MIN(duration_minutes) AS lowest_trip_duration_minutes
FROM ranked_trips
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH year_month_trips AS (
  SELECT 
    FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y%m', start_date) AS year_month,
    start_date,
    ROUND(duration_sec / 60.0, 4) AS duration_min
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    year_month,
    duration_min,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month 
      ORDER BY start_date ASC
    ) AS rn_first,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY year_month 
      ORDER BY start_date DESC
    ) AS rn_last
  FROM year_month_trips
)
SELECT 
  year_month,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn_first = 1 THEN duration_min END), 4) AS first_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN rn_last = 1 THEN duration_min END), 4) AS last_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MAX(duration_min), 4) AS highest_trip_duration_min,
  ROUND(MIN(duration_min), 4) AS lowest_trip_duration_min
FROM ranked
GROUP BY year_month
ORDER BY year_month
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH trips_filtered AS (
    SELECT 
        t."trip_id",
        t."duration_sec",
        t."start_date",
        t."start_station_name",
        t."end_station_name",
        t."bike_number",
        t."subscriber_type",
        t."member_birth_year",
        t."member_gender",
        t."start_station_id"
    FROM "SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS"."SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
    WHERE 
        t."start_date" BETWEEN 1498867200000000 AND 1514764799000000  -- July 1, 2017 00:00:00 to Dec 31, 2017 23:59:59 UTC (microseconds)
        AND t."start_station_name" IS NOT NULL AND t."start_station_name" != 'None'
        AND t."member_birth_year" IS NOT NULL AND CAST(t."member_birth_year" AS VARCHAR) != 'nan'
        AND t."member_gender" IS NOT NULL AND t."member_gender" != 'None'
),
station_info_cleaned AS (
    SELECT 
        s."station_id",
        s."name" AS "station_name",
        s."region_id"
    FROM "SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS"."SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATION_INFO" s
    WHERE s."station_id" IS NOT NULL AND s."region_id" IS NOT NULL
),
region_names AS (
    SELECT 
        r."region_id",
        r."name" AS "region_name"
    FROM "SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS"."SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_REGIONS" r
),
joined AS (
    SELECT 
        f."trip_id",
        f."duration_sec",
        f."start_date",
        f."start_station_name",
        f."end_station_name",
        f."bike_number",
        f."subscriber_type",
        f."member_birth_year",
        f."member_gender",
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - f."member_birth_year" AS "current_age",
        CASE 
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - f."member_birth_year" < 40 THEN 'Young (<40 Y.O)'
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - f."member_birth_year" BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'
            ELSE 'Senior Adult (>60 Y.O)'
        END AS "age_classification",
        f."start_station_name" || ' - ' || f."end_station_name" AS "route",
        r."region_name"
    FROM trips_filtered f
    LEFT JOIN station_info_cleaned s 
        ON CAST(f."start_station_id" AS VARCHAR) = s."station_id"
    LEFT JOIN region_names r 
        ON s."region_id" = r."region_id"
)
SELECT 
    "trip_id",
    "duration_sec",
    TO_TIMESTAMP("start_date" / 1000000) AS "start_date_timestamp",
    "start_station_name",
    "route",
    "bike_number",
    "subscriber_type",
    "member_birth_year",
    "current_age",
    "age_classification",
    "member_gender",
    "region_name"
FROM joined
ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH filtered_trips AS (
    SELECT 
        t."trip_id",
        t."duration_sec",
        TO_TIMESTAMP(t."start_date" / 1000000) AS "start_date",
        t."start_station_name",
        t."start_station_name" || ' - ' || t."end_station_name" AS "route",
        t."bike_number",
        t."subscriber_type",
        t."member_birth_year",
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") AS "age",
        CASE 
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") < 40 THEN 'Young (<40 Y.O)'
            WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_DATE) - FLOOR(t."member_birth_year") BETWEEN 40 AND 60 THEN 'Adult (40-60 Y.O)'
            ELSE 'Senior Adult (>60 Y.O)'
        END AS "age_class",
        t."member_gender",
        t."start_station_id"
    FROM SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_TRIPS t
    WHERE 
        t."start_station_name" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_birth_year" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_gender" IS NOT NULL
        AND t."member_gender" != 'None'
        AND TO_TIMESTAMP(t."start_date" / 1000000) BETWEEN '2017-07-01'::TIMESTAMP AND '2017-12-31 23:59:59'::TIMESTAMP
),
trips_with_region AS (
    SELECT 
        f."trip_id",
        f."duration_sec",
        f."start_date",
        f."start_station_name",
        f."route",
        f."bike_number",
        f."subscriber_type",
        f."member_birth_year",
        f."age",
        f."age_class",
        f."member_gender",
        r."name" AS "region_name"
    FROM filtered_trips f
    LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_STATION_INFO si
        ON CAST(f."start_station_id" AS VARCHAR) = si."station_id"
    LEFT JOIN SAN_FRANCISCO_PLUS.SAN_FRANCISCO_BIKESHARE.BIKESHARE_REGIONS r
        ON si."region_id" = r."region_id"
)
SELECT 
    "trip_id",
    "duration_sec",
    "start_date",
    "start_station_name",
    "route",
    "bike_number",
    "subscriber_type",
    "member_birth_year",
    "age",
    "age_class",
    "member_gender",
    "region_name"
FROM trips_with_region
ORDER BY "duration_sec" DESC
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
  users_2019 AS (
    SELECT
      u."id" AS "user_id",
      u."email"
    FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS u
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATEADD('microsecond', u."created_at"::NUMBER, '1970-01-01'::TIMESTAMP)) = 2019
  ),
  orders_2019 AS (
    SELECT
      o."order_id",
      o."user_id",
      o."num_of_item"
    FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS o
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM DATEADD('microsecond', o."created_at"::NUMBER, '1970-01-01'::TIMESTAMP)) = 2019
  ),
  order_value AS (
    SELECT
      o."order_id",
      o."user_id",
      o."num_of_item",
      SUM(oi."sale_price") AS "total_sale_price_per_order"
    FROM orders_2019 o
    JOIN THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS oi
      ON o."order_id" = oi."order_id"
    GROUP BY o."order_id", o."user_id", o."num_of_item"
  ),
  user_aggregated AS (
    SELECT
      ov."user_id",
      SUM(ov."total_sale_price_per_order") AS "total_order_value",
      COUNT(ov."order_id") AS "total_orders"
    FROM order_value ov
    GROUP BY ov."user_id"
    HAVING COUNT(ov."order_id") > 0
  ),
  ranked_users AS (
    SELECT
      u."email",
      ROUND((ua."total_order_value" / ua."total_orders"), 4) AS "avg_order_value",
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        ORDER BY (ua."total_order_value" / ua."total_orders") DESC,
                 ua."user_id" ASC
      ) AS "rnk"
    FROM user_aggregated ua
    JOIN users_2019 u
      ON ua."user_id" = u."user_id"
  )
SELECT
  "email",
  "avg_order_value"
FROM ranked_users
WHERE "rnk" <= 10
ORDER BY "rnk";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH users_2019 AS (
    SELECT "id", "email"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."USERS"
    WHERE "created_at" >= 1546300800000000
      AND "created_at" < 1577836800000000
),
orders_2019 AS (
    SELECT "order_id", "user_id"
    FROM "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."ORDERS"
    WHERE "created_at" >= 1546300800000000
      AND "created_at" < 1577836800000000
      AND "status" != 'Cancelled'
),
order_values AS (
    SELECT 
        o."order_id",
        o."user_id",
        SUM(oi."sale_price") AS "order_total"
    FROM orders_2019 o
    INNER JOIN "THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."THELOOK_ECOMMERCE"."ORDER_ITEMS" oi
        ON o."order_id" = oi."order_id"
    WHERE oi."status" != 'Cancelled'
    GROUP BY o."order_id", o."user_id"
),
user_avg_order_value AS (
    SELECT 
        "user_id",
        ROUND(SUM("order_total") / COUNT("order_id"), 4) AS "avg_order_value"
    FROM order_values
    GROUP BY "user_id"
)
SELECT 
    u."email"
FROM user_avg_order_value um
INNER JOIN users_2019 u ON um."user_id" = u."id"
ORDER BY um."avg_order_value" DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Calculate country-level aggregates for May 10, 2020
WITH country_aggregates AS (
    SELECT
        country_code,
        SUM(cumulative_confirmed) AS total_confirmed,
        SUM(cumulative_recovered) AS total_recovered
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
    WHERE date = '2020-05-10'
    GROUP BY country_code
    -- Only include countries with more than 50,000 confirmed cases
    HAVING SUM(cumulative_confirmed) > 50000
)
-- Select top 3 countries by recovery rate
SELECT
    country_code,
    ROUND((total_recovered / total_confirmed) * 100, 4) AS recovery_rate_percentage
FROM country_aggregates
ORDER BY recovery_rate_percentage DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
  country_name,
  ROUND(cumulative_recovered / cumulative_confirmed * 100, 2) AS recovery_rate_percentage
FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE date = '2020-05-10'
  AND subregion1_code IS NULL
  AND subregion2_code IS NULL
  AND locality_code IS NULL
  AND cumulative_confirmed > 50000
  AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
  AND cumulative_recovered IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY recovery_rate_percentage DESC
LIMIT 3
```

```sql
  WHERE table_name = 'covid19_open_data'
),

  SELECT 
    country_name,
    MAX(cumulative_confirmed) AS total_confirmed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
  WHERE date = '2020-06-30'
    AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
    AND cumulative_confirmed > 0
  GROUP BY country_name
),
-- Get population data from World Bank for 2018

  SELECT 
    country_name,
    value AS population_2018
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
  WHERE indicator_code = 'SP.POP.TOTL' 
    AND year = 2018
    AND value IS NOT NULL
    AND value > 0
)
-- Calculate percentage of population confirmed with COVID-19
SELECT 
  c.country_name,
  c.total_confirmed,
  p.population_2018,
  ROUND((c.total_confirmed / p.population_2018) * 100, 4) AS confirmed_percentage
FROM covid_cases c
INNER JOIN country_population p 
  ON LOWER(c.country_name) = LOWER(p.country_name)
ORDER BY confirmed_percentage DESC;
```

```sql
WITH
    -- Subset of national COVID-19 data for June 30, 2020
    covid AS (
        SELECT
            country_name,
            cumulative_confirmed
        FROM
            `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
        WHERE
            date = '2020-06-30'
            AND subregion1_code IS NULL
            AND subregion2_code IS NULL
            AND country_name IS NOT NULL
            AND cumulative_confirmed IS NOT NULL
    ),
    -- Subset of World Bank 2018 population data
    population AS (
        SELECT
            country,
            year_2018 AS population_2018
        FROM
            `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
        WHERE
            year_2018 IS NOT NULL
            AND country IS NOT NULL
    )
SELECT
    covid.country_name,
    ROUND(
        SAFE_DIVIDE(covid.cumulative_confirmed * 100.0, population.population_2018),
        4
    ) AS infection_percentage
FROM
    covid
    INNER JOIN population
        ON LOWER(TRIM(covid.country_name)) = LOWER(TRIM(population.country))
ORDER BY
    covid.country_name;
```

```sql
-- CTE: Total confirmed cases per country as of April 20, 2020
WITH cases AS (
  SELECT
    country_or_region,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(_4_20_20 AS INT64)) AS total_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.confirmed_cases`
  WHERE LOWER(country_or_region) IN ('us', 'france', 'china', 'italy', 'spain', 'germany', 'iran')
  GROUP BY country_or_region
),

-- Mapping from JHU CSSE country names to World Bank country names
country_mapping AS (
  SELECT 'US' AS jhu_name, 'United States' AS wb_name
  UNION ALL SELECT 'France', 'France'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'China', 'China'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Italy', 'Italy'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Spain', 'Spain'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Germany', 'Germany'
  UNION ALL SELECT 'Iran', 'Iran, Islamic Rep.'   -- World Bank uses "Iran, Islamic Rep." for Iran
),

-- Population data: total population for 2020 from World Bank (SP.POP.TOTL)
population AS (
  SELECT
    country_name,
    SUM(value) AS population
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
  WHERE indicator_code = 'SP.POP.TOTL'
    AND year = 2020
  GROUP BY country_name
)

-- Final result: country, total cases, and cases per 100,000 people
SELECT
  c.country_or_region AS country,
  c.total_cases,
  ROUND(c.total_cases * 100000.0 / p.population, 4) AS cases_per_100k
FROM cases c
JOIN country_mapping m
  ON c.country_or_region = m.jhu_name
LEFT JOIN population p
  ON m.wb_name = p.country_name
ORDER BY country;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH covid_cases AS (
  SELECT
    country_or_region,
    SUM(SAFE_CAST(_4_20_20 AS INT64)) AS total_confirmed_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.confirmed_cases`
  WHERE country_or_region IN ('US', 'France', 'China', 'Italy', 'Spain', 'Germany', 'Iran')
  GROUP BY country_or_region
),

country_population AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'US'      THEN 'USA'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'France'  THEN 'FRA'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'China'   THEN 'CHN'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Italy'   THEN 'ITA'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Spain'   THEN 'ESP'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Germany' THEN 'DEU'
      WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Iran'    THEN 'IRN'
    END AS country_code,
    covid.country_or_region,
    pop.year_2019 AS population
  FROM covid_cases AS covid
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country` AS pop
    ON pop.country_code = CASE
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'US'      THEN 'USA'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'France'  THEN 'FRA'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'China'   THEN 'CHN'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Italy'   THEN 'ITA'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Spain'   THEN 'ESP'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Germany' THEN 'DEU'
                            WHEN covid.country_or_region = 'Iran'    THEN 'IRN'
                          END
)

SELECT
  covid.country_or_region,
  covid.total_confirmed_cases,
  ROUND((covid.total_confirmed_cases / cp.population) * 100000, 4) AS cases_per_100k
FROM covid_cases AS covid
LEFT JOIN country_population AS cp
  ON covid.country_or_region = cp.country_or_region
ORDER BY covid.country_or_region;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute daily new cases (increase) for each state.
WITH state_daily AS (
    SELECT
        state_name,
        date,
        confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (
            PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date
        ) AS new_cases
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
),

-- Step 2: Filter to dates March�May 2020 and keep only valid new_cases (exclude first row of each state).
state_daily_filtered AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM state_daily
    WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
      AND new_cases IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 3: For each day, rank states by new_cases descending, pick top 5.
daily_top5_states AS (
    SELECT
        state_name,
        date,
        new_cases,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY new_cases DESC) AS rn
    FROM state_daily_filtered
)
-- Step 4: Count how many times each state appears in the daily top 5, rank overall.
, state_freq AS (
    SELECT
        state_name,
        COUNT(*) AS frequency
    FROM daily_top5_states
    WHERE rn <= 5
    GROUP BY state_name
)
, state_ranking AS (
    SELECT
        state_name,
        frequency,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS overall_rank
    FROM state_freq
)
-- Step 5: Identify the 4th ranked state.
, fourth_state AS (
    SELECT state_name
    FROM state_ranking
    WHERE overall_rank = 4
)

-- Now for counties of that state.
-- Step 6: Compute daily new cases for each county in that state.
, county_daily AS (
    SELECT
        c.state_name,
        c.county,
        c.county_fips_code,
        c.date,
        c.confirmed_cases - LAG(c.confirmed_cases) OVER (
            PARTITION BY c.county_fips_code ORDER BY c.date
        ) AS new_cases
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` c
    INNER JOIN fourth_state s ON c.state_name = s.state_name
)
, county_daily_filtered AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM county_daily
    WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
      AND new_cases IS NOT NULL
)
-- Step 7: For each day, rank counties within the state by new_cases, pick top 5.
, daily_top5_counties AS (
    SELECT
        county,
        date,
        new_cases,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY new_cases DESC) AS rn
    FROM county_daily_filtered
)
-- Step 8: Count frequency of each county appearing in the daily top 5, pick top 5.
, county_freq AS (
    SELECT
        county,
        COUNT(*) AS frequency
    FROM daily_top5_counties
    WHERE rn <= 5
    GROUP BY county
)
SELECT
    county,
    frequency,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY frequency DESC) AS county_rank
FROM county_freq
ORDER BY county_rank
LIMIT 5;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH state_daily_new AS (
  -- Step 1: Compute daily new confirmed cases per state
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    date,
    confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),
state_daily_ranked AS (
  -- Step 2: Rank states by daily new cases per day, keep top 5
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new_cases,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS day_rank
  FROM state_daily_new
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL AND daily_new_cases >= 0
),
state_top5_daily AS (
  -- Keep only the top 5 states for each day based on daily new cases
  SELECT state_name, date
  FROM state_daily_ranked
  WHERE day_rank <= 5
),
state_appearance_freq AS (
  -- Step 3: Count how many times each state appears in the daily top 5
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
  FROM state_top5_daily
  GROUP BY state_name
),
state_overall_rank AS (
  -- Step 4: Rank states by their appearance frequency (highest first)
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    appearance_count,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY appearance_count DESC) AS overall_rank
  FROM state_appearance_freq
),
target_state AS (
  -- Step 5: Identify the state that ranks 4th overall
  SELECT state_name FROM state_overall_rank WHERE overall_rank = 4
),
county_daily_new AS (
  -- Step 6: Compute daily new confirmed cases per county for the target state only
  SELECT 
    c.county,
    c.state_name,
    c.date,
    c.confirmed_cases - LAG(c.confirmed_cases, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY c.county, c.state_name ORDER BY c.date) AS daily_new_cases
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` c
  INNER JOIN target_state t ON c.state_name = t.state_name
  WHERE c.date BETWEEN '2020-03-01' AND '2020-05-31'
),
county_daily_ranked AS (
  -- Step 7: Rank counties by daily new cases per day
  SELECT 
    county,
    state_name,
    date,
    daily_new_cases,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY daily_new_cases DESC) AS day_rank
  FROM county_daily_new
  WHERE daily_new_cases IS NOT NULL AND daily_new_cases >= 0
),
county_top5_daily AS (
  -- Step 8: Keep only the top 5 counties for each day
  SELECT county, state_name, date
  FROM county_daily_ranked
  WHERE day_rank <= 5
),
county_appearance_freq AS (
  -- Step 9: Count how many times each county appears in the daily top 5
  SELECT 
    county,
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
  FROM county_top5_daily
  GROUP BY county, state_name
)
-- Step 10: Return the top 5 counties by appearance frequency
SELECT 
  county,
  appearance_count
FROM county_appearance_freq
ORDER BY appearance_count DESC
LIMIT 5
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter the play-by-play data to include only shots before March 15, 2018,
--         with non-null shot_type and coordinates, and where the shot location is
--         on the correct side of the court given the team's basket.
-- Step 2: Adjust coordinates using the provided transformation to normalize all shots
--         to a consistent orientation (assuming the attacked basket is on the left).
-- Step 3: Group by shot_type and compute:
--         - average adjusted x and y coordinates
--         - total number of shot attempts (count of rows)
--         - total number of successful shots (sum of shot_made as integer)
WITH filtered_shots AS (
  SELECT
    shot_type,
    event_coord_x,
    event_coord_y,
    shot_made,
    -- Determine if this shot is on the correct side of the court
    (team_basket = 'left' AND event_coord_x > 564) OR
    (team_basket = 'right' AND event_coord_x < 564) AS is_correct_side
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
  WHERE
    shot_type IS NOT NULL
    AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
    AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
    AND scheduled_date < TIMESTAMP('2018-03-15 00:00:00+00')
),
valid_shots AS (
  SELECT
    shot_type,
    -- Adjusted X coordinate
    CASE
      WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
      ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
    END AS adj_x,
    -- Adjusted Y coordinate
    CASE
      WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
      ELSE event_coord_y
    END AS adj_y,
    -- Convert boolean to integer for counting successes
    CAST(shot_made AS INT64) AS made
  FROM filtered_shots
  WHERE is_correct_side = TRUE
)
SELECT
  shot_type,
  ROUND(AVG(adj_x), 4) AS avg_adj_x,
  ROUND(AVG(adj_y), 4) AS avg_adj_y,
  COUNT(*) AS total_attempts,
  SUM(made) AS total_successful
FROM valid_shots
GROUP BY shot_type
ORDER BY shot_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Filter and prepare all valid shots, with a date range to reduce scanned bytes
  filtered_shots AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      -- Adjust X: mirror right-side shots to left-side orientation
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN event_coord_x
        ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
      END AS adjusted_x,
      -- Adjust Y: mirror accordingly based on which half the shot was on
      CASE
        WHEN event_coord_x < 564 THEN 600 - event_coord_y
        ELSE event_coord_y
      END AS adjusted_y,
      shot_made,
      game_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
    WHERE
      -- Exclude null or 'None' shot types
      shot_type IS NOT NULL
      AND shot_type != 'None'
      -- Exclude null coordinates
      AND event_coord_x IS NOT NULL
      AND event_coord_y IS NOT NULL
      -- Shots before March 15, 2018, and after a reasonable lower bound to limit data scan
      AND scheduled_date >= '2017-01-01'
      AND scheduled_date < '2018-03-15'
      -- Ensure shots are on the correct side of the court based on team's basket
      AND (
        (team_basket = 'left' AND event_coord_x < 564)
        OR (team_basket = 'right' AND event_coord_x >= 564)
      )
  ),

  -- Step 2: Per-game counts of attempts and made shots for each shot type
  per_game_counts AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      game_id,
      COUNT(*) AS shot_attempts,
      COUNTIF(shot_made) AS shots_made
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type, game_id
  ),

  -- Step 3: Overall average coordinates per shot type (across all individual shots)
  coord_averages AS (
    SELECT
      shot_type,
      AVG(adjusted_x) AS avg_adjusted_x,
      AVG(adjusted_y) AS avg_adjusted_y
    FROM filtered_shots
    GROUP BY shot_type
  )

-- Step 4: Combine coordinate averages with per-game averages
SELECT
  c.shot_type,
  ROUND(c.avg_adjusted_x, 4) AS avg_adjusted_x,
  ROUND(c.avg_adjusted_y, 4) AS avg_adjusted_y,
  ROUND(AVG(p.shot_attempts), 4) AS avg_shot_attempts,
  ROUND(AVG(p.shots_made), 4) AS avg_shots_made
FROM coord_averages c
JOIN per_game_counts p
  ON c.shot_type = p.shot_type
GROUP BY c.shot_type, c.avg_adjusted_x, c.avg_adjusted_y
ORDER BY c.shot_type;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Create CTE for historical tournament games (season >= 2014)
WITH historical_games AS (
  -- Winning team row
  SELECT
    academic_year AS season,
    'win' AS label,
    win_seed AS seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014

  UNION ALL

  -- Losing team row
  SELECT
    academic_year AS season,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_seed AS seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year >= 2014
),

-- Step 2: CTE for 2018 tournament results (already has win/loss per team)
results_2018 AS (
  SELECT
    season,
    label,
    seed,
    school_ncaa,
    opponent_seed,
    opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
  WHERE season = 2018
),

-- Step 3: Union all games
all_games AS (
  SELECT * FROM historical_games
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM results_2018
)

-- Step 4: Join feature engineering for team and opponent metrics
SELECT
  a.season,
  a.label,
  a.seed,
  a.school_ncaa,
  a.opponent_seed,
  a.opponent_school_ncaa,
  -- Team metrics
  team.pace_rank AS pace_rank,
  team.poss_40min AS poss_40min,
  team.pace_rating AS pace_rating,
  team.efficiency_rank AS efficiency_rank,
  team.pts_100poss AS pts_100poss,
  team.efficiency_rating AS efficiency_rating,
  -- Opponent metrics
  opp.pace_rank AS opp_pace_rank,
  opp.poss_40min AS opp_poss_40min,
  opp.pace_rating AS opp_pace_rating,
  opp.efficiency_rank AS opp_efficiency_rank,
  opp.pts_100poss AS opp_pts_100poss,
  opp.efficiency_rating AS opp_efficiency_rating,
  -- Differences (opponent - team)
  opp.pace_rank - team.pace_rank AS pace_rank_diff,
  opp.poss_40min - team.poss_40min AS pace_stat_diff,
  opp.pace_rating - team.pace_rating AS pace_rating_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rank - team.efficiency_rank AS eff_rank_diff,
  opp.pts_100poss - team.pts_100poss AS eff_stat_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rating - team.efficiency_rating AS eff_rating_diff
FROM all_games a
INNER JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` team
  ON a.season = team.season
  AND a.school_ncaa = team.team
INNER JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` opp
  ON a.season = opp.season
  AND a.opponent_school_ncaa = opp.team
ORDER BY a.season, a.label, a.school_ncaa;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH historical_games AS (
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    'win' AS label,
    win_seed AS seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    lose_seed AS opponent_seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year BETWEEN 2014 AND 2017
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    academic_year AS season,
    'loss' AS label,
    lose_seed AS seed,
    lose_school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
    win_seed AS opponent_seed,
    win_school_ncaa AS opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_historical_tournament_games`
  WHERE academic_year BETWEEN 2014 AND 2017
),

games_2018 AS (
  SELECT 
    season,
    label,
    seed,
    school_ncaa,
    opponent_seed,
    opponent_school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
  WHERE season = 2018
),

all_games AS (
  SELECT * FROM historical_games
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM games_2018
),

-- Pre-filter feature_engineering to relevant seasons only
filtered_features AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering`
  WHERE season >= 2014
)

SELECT 
  g.season,
  g.label,
  g.seed,
  g.school_ncaa,
  g.opponent_seed,
  g.opponent_school_ncaa,
  tm.pace_rank,
  tm.poss_40min,
  tm.pace_rating,
  tm.efficiency_rank,
  tm.pts_100poss,
  tm.efficiency_rating,
  opp.pace_rank AS opp_pace_rank,
  opp.poss_40min AS opp_poss_40min,
  opp.pace_rating AS opp_pace_rating,
  opp.efficiency_rank AS opp_efficiency_rank,
  opp.pts_100poss AS opp_pts_100poss,
  opp.efficiency_rating AS opp_efficiency_rating,
  opp.pace_rank - tm.pace_rank AS pace_rank_diff,
  opp.poss_40min - tm.poss_40min AS pace_stat_diff,
  opp.pace_rating - tm.pace_rating AS pace_rating_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rank - tm.efficiency_rank AS eff_rank_diff,
  opp.pts_100poss - tm.pts_100poss AS eff_stat_diff,
  opp.efficiency_rating - tm.efficiency_rating AS eff_rating_diff
FROM all_games g
LEFT JOIN filtered_features tm
  ON g.school_ncaa = tm.team AND g.season = tm.season
LEFT JOIN filtered_features opp
  ON g.opponent_school_ncaa = opp.team AND g.season = opp.season
ORDER BY g.season, g.school_ncaa;
```
</details>

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Combined 2021 report comparing racial (Asian, Black, Hispanic/Latinx, White) and gender (Women, Men) distributions
-- across Google's overall workforce hiring, Google's overall workforce representation, and BLS technology sectors.
-- Uses non-intersectional tables for simpler race and gender breakdowns.
-- BLS technology sectors: "Internet publishing and broadcasting and web search portals" and "Computer systems design and related services"
-- Weighted averages are computed for BLS data based on total employed.

WITH
-- Google: Overall workforce hiring (non-intersectional) for 2021
google_hiring AS (
  SELECT
    race_asian,
    race_black,
    race_hispanic_latinx,
    race_white,
    gender_us_women,
    gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_hiring`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND LOWER(workforce) = 'overall'
  LIMIT 1  -- ensures single row if multiple exist
),

-- Google: Overall workforce representation (non-intersectional) for 2021
google_representation AS (
  SELECT
    race_asian,
    race_black,
    race_hispanic_latinx,
    race_white,
    gender_us_women,
    gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND LOWER(workforce) = 'overall'
  LIMIT 1
),

-- BLS: Technology sectors filtered by subsector (Internet publishing / web search portals / Computer systems design)
bls_raw AS (
  SELECT
    subsector,
    total_employed_in_thousands,
    percent_asian,
    percent_black_or_african_american,
    percent_hispanic_or_latino,
    percent_white,
    percent_women
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.cpsaat18`
  WHERE year = 2021
    AND (
      LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%internet publishing%'
      OR LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%web search portals%'
      OR LOWER(subsector) LIKE '%computer systems design%'
    )
),

-- Compute weighted averages for BLS percentages across the matching subsectors
bls_weighted AS (
  SELECT
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      SUM(percent_asian * total_employed_in_thousands),
      SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
    ) AS percent_asian,
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      SUM(percent_black_or_african_american * total_employed_in_thousands),
      SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
    ) AS percent_black,
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      SUM(percent_hispanic_or_latino * total_employed_in_thousands),
      SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
    ) AS percent_hispanic_latinx,
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      SUM(percent_white * total_employed_in_thousands),
      SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
    ) AS percent_white,
    SAFE_DIVIDE(
      SUM(percent_women * total_employed_in_thousands),
      SUM(total_employed_in_thousands)
    ) AS percent_women
  FROM bls_raw
)

-- Final combined output: one row per category
SELECT
  'Asian' AS category,
  ROUND(h.race_asian, 4) AS hiring_percentage,
  ROUND(r.race_asian, 4) AS representation_percentage,
  ROUND(b.percent_asian, 4) AS bls_percentage
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_weighted b

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'Black',
  ROUND(h.race_black, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_black, 4),
  ROUND(b.percent_black, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_weighted b

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'Hispanic/Latinx',
  ROUND(h.race_hispanic_latinx, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_hispanic_latinx, 4),
  ROUND(b.percent_hispanic_latinx, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_weighted b

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'White',
  ROUND(h.race_white, 4),
  ROUND(r.race_white, 4),
  ROUND(b.percent_white, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_weighted b

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'Women',
  ROUND(h.gender_us_women, 4),
  ROUND(r.gender_us_women, 4),
  ROUND(b.percent_women, 4)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_weighted b

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'Men',
  ROUND(h.gender_us_men, 4),
  ROUND(r.gender_us_men, 4),
  ROUND(1.0 - b.percent_women, 4)  -- BLS only provides women; men derived as complement (assumes binary)
FROM google_hiring h, google_representation r, bls_weighted b

ORDER BY category;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Combined 2021 Report: Google Hiring, Google Representation, and BLS Tech Sectors
-- Fixed BLS table reference using wildcard to locate the correct 2021 table

WITH google_hiring AS (
  SELECT
    'Google Hiring' AS source,
    ROUND(race_asian, 4) AS race_asian,
    ROUND(race_black, 4) AS race_black,
    ROUND(race_hispanic_latinx, 4) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
    ROUND(race_white, 4) AS race_white,
    ROUND(gender_us_women, 4) AS gender_us_women,
    ROUND(gender_us_men, 4) AS gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_hiring`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND workforce = 'overall'
),

google_representation AS (
  SELECT
    'Google Representation' AS source,
    ROUND(race_asian, 4) AS race_asian,
    ROUND(race_black, 4) AS race_black,
    ROUND(race_hispanic_latinx, 4) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
    ROUND(race_white, 4) AS race_white,
    ROUND(gender_us_women, 4) AS gender_us_women,
    ROUND(gender_us_men, 4) AS gender_us_men
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
  WHERE report_year = 2021
    AND workforce = 'overall'
),

bls_tech_raw AS (
  -- Use wildcard table with _TABLE_SUFFIX to find the correct 2021 BLS table
  SELECT
    percent_asian,
    percent_black_or_african_american AS percent_black,
    percent_hispanic_or_latino AS percent_hispanic_latinx,
    percent_white,
    percent_women,
    total_employed_in_thousands
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.bls.cpsaat*`
  WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX LIKE '%21%'
    AND year = 2021
    AND (
      LOWER(sector) LIKE '%internet publishing%'
      OR LOWER(sector) LIKE '%web search portals%'
      OR LOWER(sector) LIKE '%computer systems design%'
      OR LOWER(sector) LIKE '%related services%'
    )
),

-- Aggregate BLS sectors into one row; convert percentages (0-100) to proportions
bls_tech AS (
  SELECT
    'BLS Tech Sectors' AS source,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_asian) / 100, 4) AS race_asian,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_black) / 100, 4) AS race_black,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_hispanic_latinx) / 100, 4) AS race_hispanic_latinx,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_white) / 100, 4) AS race_white,
    ROUND(AVG(percent_women) / 100, 4) AS gender_us_women,
    ROUND(1 - (AVG(percent_women) / 100), 4) AS gender_us_men
  FROM bls_tech_raw
)

-- Final combined report
SELECT * FROM google_hiring
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM google_representation
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM bls_tech
ORDER BY source;
```

```sql
WITH usdt_transfers AS (
    SELECT
        l."block_number",
        -- Extract source address from topics[1]: remove 12 leading zero bytes, keep last 20 bytes (40 hex chars)
        '0x' || RIGHT(PARSE_JSON(l."topics")[1]::STRING, 40) AS "source_address",
        -- Extract destination address from topics[2]
        '0x' || RIGHT(PARSE_JSON(l."topics")[2]::STRING, 40) AS "destination_address",
        -- Convert hex data (e.g., '0x000�0b06e040') to decimal number
        -- Steps: strip '0x', remove leading zeros, take at most 38 hex digits (fits Snowflake NUMBER precision), then convert
        COALESCE(
            TRY_TO_NUMBER(
                RIGHT(LTRIM(SUBSTRING(l."data", 3), '0'), 38),
                'XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX'
            ),
            0
        ) AS "raw_value"
    FROM "GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN"."GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_TRON_MAINNET_US"."LOGS" l
    WHERE l."address" = '0xa614f803b6fd780986a42c78ec9c7f77e6ded13c'               -- USDT contract
      AND PARSE_JSON(l."topics")[0]::STRING = '0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef'  -- Transfer event
)
SELECT
    u."block_number",
    u."source_address",
    u."destination_address",
    ROUND(u."raw_value" / 1000000, 4) AS "transfer_amount"
FROM usdt_transfers u
ORDER BY "transfer_amount" DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
WITH parsed_logs AS (
    SELECT
        "block_number",
        "data",
        TRY_PARSE_JSON("topics") AS topics_json
    FROM "GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN"."GOOG_BLOCKCHAIN_TRON_MAINNET_US"."LOGS"
    WHERE "address" = '0xa614f803b6fd780986a42c78ec9c7f77e6ded13c'
      AND TRY_PARSE_JSON("topics")[0]::STRING = '0xddf252ad1be2c89b69c2b068fc378daa952ba7f163c4a11628f55a4df523b3ef'
      AND "removed" = FALSE
),

extracted AS (
    SELECT
        "block_number",
        '0x' || RIGHT(SUBSTRING(topics_json[1]::STRING, 3), 40) AS "source_hex",
        '0x' || RIGHT(SUBSTRING(topics_json[2]::STRING, 3), 40) AS "dest_hex",
        LTRIM(SUBSTRING("data", 3), '0') AS "raw_amount_hex"
    FROM parsed_logs
),

converted AS (
    SELECT
        "block_number",
        "source_hex",
        "dest_hex",
        ROUND(
            TRY_CAST('0x' || COALESCE(NULLIF("raw_amount_hex", ''), '0') AS DOUBLE) / 1000000,
            4
        ) AS "transfer_amount"
    FROM extracted
)

SELECT
    "block_number",
    "source_hex" AS "source_address",
    "dest_hex" AS "destination_address",
    "transfer_amount"
FROM converted
WHERE "transfer_amount" IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY "transfer_amount" DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Count motor vehicle theft incidents per month in 2016
WITH monthly_counts AS (
  SELECT
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS incident_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  WHERE
    primary_type = 'MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT'
    AND year = 2016  -- Fast filter using the dedicated year column
  GROUP BY
    month
)
-- Step 2: Get the highest count among all months
SELECT
  MAX(incident_count) AS highest_monthly_count
FROM
  monthly_counts;
```

```sql
  SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC(date, MONTH) AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS monthly_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2016-01-01' AND '2016-12-31'
    AND primary_type = 'MOTOR VEHICLE THEFT'
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT MAX(monthly_count) AS max_motor_vehicle_theft_monthly
FROM monthly_counts;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify drug IDs for the four specified trade names from MOLECULE table
WITH target_drugs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m."id" AS drug_id
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1.PLATFORM.MOLECULE m,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => m."tradeNames":"list") tn
    WHERE tn."VALUE":"element"::VARCHAR IN ('Keytruda', 'Vioxx', 'Premarin', 'Humira')
),

-- Step 2: Find drugs that have a black box warning
black_box_drugs AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT c."VALUE":"element"::VARCHAR AS drug_id
    FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1.PLATFORM.DRUGWARNINGS dw,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => dw."chemblIds":"list") c
    WHERE dw."warningType" = 'Black Box Warning'
)

-- Step 3: Retrieve detailed molecule data for approved drugs meeting all criteria
SELECT
    m."id" AS drug_id,
    m."drugType" AS drug_type,
    m."hasBeenWithdrawn" AS withdrawal_status
FROM OPEN_TARGETS_PLATFORM_1.PLATFORM.MOLECULE m
WHERE m."isApproved" = TRUE
  AND m."drugType" IS NOT NULL
  AND m."id" IN (SELECT drug_id FROM target_drugs)
  AND m."id" IN (SELECT drug_id FROM black_box_drugs);
```

```sql
  WHERE k."tradeNames" IS NOT NULL
    AND LOWER(TRIM(f.value:"element"::STRING)) IN ('keytruda', 'vioxx', 'premarin', 'humira')
)
SELECT

  m."hasBeenWithdrawn" AS "withdrawal_status"
```

```sql
  ROUND(MAX(coloc_log2_h4_h3) - MIN(coloc_log2_h4_h3), 4) AS max_min_diff,
```

```sql
  WHERE 
    vdc.coloc_h4 > 0.8
    AND vdc.coloc_h3 < 0.02
    AND vdc.right_bio_feature = 'IPSC'
    AND vdc.left_chrom = '1'
    AND vdc.left_pos = 55029009
    AND vdc.left_ref = 'C'
    AND vdc.left_alt = 'T'
),
max_row AS (
  SELECT right_study
  FROM filtered_data
  ORDER BY coloc_log2_h4_h3 DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  ROUND(AVG(coloc_log2_h4_h3), 4) AS avg_log2_h4_h3,
  ROUND(VARIANCE(coloc_log2_h4_h3), 4) AS variance_log2_h4_h3,
  ROUND(MAX(coloc_log2_h4_h3) - MIN(coloc_log2_h4_h3), 4) AS max_min_diff_log2_h4_h3,
  (SELECT right_study FROM max_row) AS qtl_source_of_max
FROM filtered_data;
```
</details>

### 36. bq090 (DB: `CYMBAL_INVESTMENTS`)
**Question**: How much higher the average intrinsic value is for trades using the feeling-lucky strategy compared to those using the momentum strategy under long-side trades?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

|   AVG_INTRINSIC_VALUE_DIFFERENCE |
|---------------------------------:|
|                         -0.27641 |

**OR**

|   DIFFERENCE |
|-------------:|
|      0.27641 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   difference |
|-------------:|
|       0.0013 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   avg_intrinsic_value_higher_for_feeling_lucky |
|-----------------------------------------------:|
|                                         0.0255 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Define CTE to filter long-side trades and compute intrinsic value and strategy
WITH long_trades AS (
  SELECT
    StrikePrice,
    LastPx,
    -- Intrinsic value: profit if closed at strike price (for long CFD)
    StrikePrice - LastPx AS intrinsic_value,
    -- Determine strategy based on TargetCompID pattern
    CASE
      WHEN LOWER(TargetCompID) LIKE '%momo%' THEN 'momentum'
      ELSE 'feeling-lucky'
    END AS strategy
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`
  WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM UNNEST(Sides) AS side_struct
    WHERE side_struct.Side = 'LONG'
  )
),
-- Step 2: Compute average intrinsic value per strategy
avg_by_strategy AS (
  SELECT
    strategy,
    AVG(intrinsic_value) AS avg_intrinsic
  FROM long_trades
  WHERE strategy IN ('momentum', 'feeling-lucky')  -- ensure only these two
  GROUP BY strategy
),
-- Step 3: Pivot the averages to calculate the difference
diff AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN strategy = 'feeling-lucky' THEN avg_intrinsic END) -
    MAX(CASE WHEN strategy = 'momentum' THEN avg_intrinsic END) AS difference
  FROM avg_by_strategy
)
-- Step 4: Output the rounded result
SELECT ROUND(difference, 4) AS avg_intrinsic_value_higher_for_feeling_lucky
FROM diff;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH long_trades AS (
  SELECT
    t.StrikePrice,
    t.LastPx,
    t.StrikePrice - t.LastPx AS intrinsic_value,
    CASE
      WHEN t.TargetCompID LIKE '%MOMOES%' THEN 'momentum'
      WHEN t.TargetCompID LIKE '%LUCKY%' THEN 'feeling-lucky'
      ELSE NULL
    END AS strategy
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` AS t,
  UNNEST(t.Sides) AS side
  WHERE side.Side = 'LONG'
    AND (t.TargetCompID LIKE '%MOMOES%' OR t.TargetCompID LIKE '%LUCKY%')
),
avg_intrinsic AS (
  SELECT
    strategy,
    ROUND(AVG(intrinsic_value), 4) AS avg_value
  FROM long_trades
  WHERE strategy IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY strategy
)
SELECT
  ROUND(
    (SELECT avg_value FROM avg_intrinsic WHERE strategy = 'feeling-lucky') -
    (SELECT avg_value FROM avg_intrinsic WHERE strategy = 'momentum'),
    4
  ) AS difference;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Filter ports in region 6585 within US
"ports_in_region" AS (
    SELECT 
        p."port_name",
        p."port_latitude",
        p."port_longitude",
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(p."port_geom") AS "port_geom",
        p."country",
        p."region_number"
    FROM "NOAA_PORTS"."GEO_INTERNATIONAL_PORTS"."WORLD_PORT_INDEX" p
    WHERE p."region_number" = '6585'
      AND p."country" = 'US'
),

-- US states boundaries
"us_states" AS (
    SELECT 
        s."state_name",
        s."state",
        ST_GEOGFROMWKB(s."state_geom") AS "state_geom"
    FROM "NOAA_PORTS"."GEO_US_BOUNDARIES"."STATES" s
),

-- Ports within US state boundaries
"ports_within_us" AS (
    SELECT 
        pr."port_name",
        pr."port_latitude",
        pr."port_longitude",
        pr."port_geom",
        us."state_name",
        us."state"
    FROM "ports_in_region" pr
    INNER JOIN "us_states" us ON ST_WITHIN(pr."port_geom", us."state_geom")
),

-- Filtered North Atlantic storms (wind >= 35 knots, sshs >= 0)
"na_storms" AS (
    SELECT 
        h."sid",
        h."season",
        h."usa_wind",
        h."usa_sshs",
        h."latitude",
        h."longitude",
        h."usa_status",
        h."usa_r34_ne",
        h."usa_r34_nw",
        h."usa_r34_se",
        h."usa_r34_sw"
    FROM "NOAA_PORTS"."NOAA_HURRICANES"."HURRICANES" h
    WHERE h."basin" = 'NA'
      AND h."usa_wind" >= 35
      AND h."usa_sshs" >= 0
),

-- Create storm geometry points
"storm_geometries" AS (
    SELECT 
        ns."sid",
        ns."season",
        ns."usa_wind",
        ns."usa_sshs",
        ns."latitude",
        ns."longitude",
        ST_MAKEPOINT(ns."longitude", ns."latitude") AS "storm_point"
    FROM "na_storms" ns
),

-- Link ports to storms that affected them (within 100 nautical miles)
"port_storm_links" AS (
    SELECT 
        pw."port_name",
        pw."state_name",
        pw."port_geom",
        sg."sid",
        sg."season",
        sg."usa_wind",
        sg."usa_sshs",
        sg."storm_point",
        ST_ASWKB(sg."storm_point") AS "storm_point_wkb"
    FROM "ports_within_us" pw
    INNER JOIN "storm_geometries" sg 
        ON ST_DWITHIN(pw."port_geom", sg."storm_point", 185200)
),

-- Aggregate per port
"port_aggregated" AS (
    SELECT 
        pl."port_name",
        pl."state_name",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT pl."season", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY pl."season") AS "storm_years",
        COUNT(DISTINCT pl."sid") AS "total_distinct_storms",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT pl."sid", ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY pl."sid") AS "distinct_storm_ids",
        ROUND(AVG(pl."usa_sshs"), 4) AS "avg_storm_category",
        ROUND(AVG(pl."usa_wind"), 4) AS "avg_wind_speed",
        ANY_VALUE(pl."port_geom") AS "port_geometry",
        ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT pl."storm_point_wkb") AS "storm_area_points_wkb"
    FROM "port_storm_links" pl
    GROUP BY pl."port_name", pl."state_name"
)

-- Final selection
SELECT 
    pa."port_name",
    pa."state_name",
    pa."storm_years",
    pa."total_distinct_storms",
    pa."distinct_storm_ids" AS "distinct_storm_names",
    pa."avg_storm_category",
    pa."avg_wind_speed",
    pa."port_geometry",
    pa."storm_area_points_wkb" AS "storm_geometries"
FROM "port_aggregated" pa
WHERE pa."total_distinct_storms" > 0
ORDER BY pa."state_name", pa."port_name";
```

### 38. bq277 (DB: `noaa_ports`)

```sql
WITH
  storm_obs AS (
    SELECT
      name,
      latitude,
      longitude,
      usa_r34_ne,
      usa_r34_se,
      usa_r34_sw,
      usa_r34_nw
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
    WHERE
      basin = 'NA'
      AND name IS NOT NULL
      AND name != 'NOT_NAMED'
      AND usa_wind >= 35
      AND usa_r34_ne IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_se IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_sw IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_nw IS NOT NULL
  ),
  storm_polygons AS (
    SELECT
      name,
      ST_MAKEPOLYGON(
        ST_MAKELINE(
          ST_MAKELINE(
            ST_MAKELINE(
              ST_MAKELINE(
                ST_GEOGPOINT(
                  57.2958 * (
                    longitude * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
                      SIN(45 * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)),
                      COS(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
                        57.2958 * ASIN(
                          SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                          COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(45 * (3.14159 / 180))
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  ),
                  57.2958 * ASIN(
                    SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                    COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(45 * (3.14159 / 180))
                  )
                ),
                ST_GEOGPOINT(
                  57.2958 * (
                    longitude * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
                      SIN(135 * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_se * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)),
                      COS(usa_r34_se * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
                        57.2958 * ASIN(
                          SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_se * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                          COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_se * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(135 * (3.14159 / 180))
                        )
                      )
                    )
                  ),
                  57.2958 * ASIN(
                    SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_se * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                    COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_se * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(135 * (3.14159 / 180))
                  )
                )
              ),
              ST_GEOGPOINT(
                57.2958 * (
                  longitude * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
                    SIN(225 * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_sw * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)),
                    COS(usa_r34_sw * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
                      57.2958 * ASIN(
                        SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_sw * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                        COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_sw * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(225 * (3.14159 / 180))
                      )
                    )
                  )
                ),
                57.2958 * ASIN(
                  SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_sw * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                  COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_sw * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(225 * (3.14159 / 180))
                )
              )
            ),
            ST_GEOGPOINT(
              57.2958 * (
                longitude * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
                  SIN(315 * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_nw * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)),
                  COS(usa_r34_nw * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
                    57.2958 * ASIN(
                      SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_nw * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                      COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_nw * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(315 * (3.14159 / 180))
                    )
                  )
                )
              ),
              57.2958 * ASIN(
                SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_nw * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_nw * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(315 * (3.14159 / 180))
              )
            )
          ),
          ST_GEOGPOINT(
            57.2958 * (
              longitude * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
                SIN(45 * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)),
                COS(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
                  57.2958 * ASIN(
                    SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
                    COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(45 * (3.14159 / 180))
                  )
                )
              )
            ),
            57.2958 * ASIN(
              SIN(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
              COS(latitude * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(usa_r34_ne * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(45 * (3.14159 / 180))
            )
          )
        )
      ) AS storm_area
    FROM storm_obs
  ),
  candidate_ports AS (
    SELECT p.port_name, p.port_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_international_ports.world_port_index` AS p
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states` AS s
      ON ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, s.state_geom)
    WHERE p.region_number = '6585'
  )
SELECT
  cp.port_name,
  COUNT(*) AS frequency
FROM candidate_ports AS cp
JOIN storm_polygons AS sp
  ON ST_WITHIN(cp.port_geom, sp.storm_area)
GROUP BY cp.port_name
ORDER BY frequency DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

```sql
-- Define temporary functions as required
CREATE TEMP FUNCTION nautical_miles_conversion(input_nautical_miles FLOAT64)
RETURNS FLOAT64
AS (
  input_nautical_miles * 1.15078
);

CREATE TEMP FUNCTION azimuth_to_geog_point(input_lat FLOAT64, input_lon FLOAT64, azimuth FLOAT64, distance FLOAT64)
RETURNS GEOGRAPHY
AS (
  ST_GEOGPOINT(
    57.2958 * (
      input_lon * (3.14159 / 180) + ATAN2(
        SIN(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)),
        COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) - SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(
          57.2958 * ASIN(
            SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
            COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180))
          )
        )
      )
    ),
    57.2958 * ASIN(
      SIN(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * COS(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) +
      COS(input_lat * (3.14159 / 180)) * SIN(distance * 1.61 / 6378.1) * COS(azimuth * (3.14159 / 180))
    )
  )
);

  hurricane_obs AS (
    SELECT
      sid,
      name,
      latitude,
      longitude,
      usa_wind,
      usa_r34_ne,
      usa_r34_se,
      usa_r34_sw,
      usa_r34_nw
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
    WHERE basin = 'NA'
      AND name != 'NOT_NAMED'
      AND usa_wind >= 35
      AND usa_r34_ne IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_se IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_sw IS NOT NULL
      AND usa_r34_nw IS NOT NULL
  ),
  -- Build polygons representing the 34-kt wind field (four quadrant points)
  storm_polygons AS (
    SELECT
      sid,
      name,
      latitude,
      longitude,
      usa_wind,
      ST_MAKEPOLYGON(
        -- Build a closed linestring: p1 -> p2 -> p3 -> p4 -> p1
        ST_MAKELINE(
          ST_MAKELINE(
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 45, usa_r34_ne),
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 135, usa_r34_se)
          ),
          ST_MAKELINE(
            azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 225, usa_r34_sw),
            ST_MAKELINE(
              azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 315, usa_r34_nw),
              azimuth_to_geog_point(latitude, longitude, 45, usa_r34_ne)  -- close the loop
            )
          )
        )
      ) AS storm_area
    FROM hurricane_obs
  ),
  -- U.S. states (50 states + DC)
  us_states AS (
    SELECT state_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states`
    WHERE state_name IN (
      'Alabama','Alaska','Arizona','Arkansas','California','Colorado','Connecticut','Delaware',
      'Florida','Georgia','Hawaii','Idaho','Illinois','Indiana','Iowa','Kansas','Kentucky',
      'Louisiana','Maine','Maryland','Massachusetts','Michigan','Minnesota','Mississippi',
      'Missouri','Montana','Nebraska','Nevada','New Hampshire','New Jersey','New Mexico',
      'New York','North Carolina','North Dakota','Ohio','Oklahoma','Oregon','Pennsylvania',
      'Rhode Island','South Carolina','South Dakota','Tennessee','Texas','Utah','Vermont',
      'Virginia','Washington','West Virginia','Wisconsin','Wyoming','District of Columbia'
    )
  ),
  -- Ports with region_number '6585' that lie within a U.S. state boundary
  ports_in_us AS (
    SELECT
      p.port_name,
      ANY_VALUE(p.port_geom) AS port_geom
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.geo_international_ports.world_port_index` p
    CROSS JOIN us_states s
    WHERE p.region_number = '6585'
      AND ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, s.state_geom)
    GROUP BY p.port_name
  ),
  -- Count how many storm polygons contain each port
  port_storm_counts AS (
    SELECT
      p.port_name,
      COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM ports_in_us p
    JOIN storm_polygons sp
      ON ST_WITHIN(p.port_geom, sp.storm_area)
    GROUP BY p.port_name
  )
-- Return the port with the highest count
SELECT port_name
FROM port_storm_counts
ORDER BY cnt DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Aggregate census tract level data to state level
tract_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS tract_count,
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified_buildings_tract,
    AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_percent_covered_tract,
    AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_percent_qualified_tract,
    SUM(number_of_panels_total) AS total_panels_tract,
    SUM(kw_total) AS total_kw_tract,
    SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total) AS total_yearly_sunlight_kwh_tract,
    SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons) AS total_carbon_offset_tract,
    SUM(existing_installs_count) AS total_existing_installs_tract,
    -- Calculate total qualified buildings at tract level by summing count_qualified (already covered & qualified)
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified_tract
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
  GROUP BY state_name
),

-- Aggregate postal code level data to state level
postal_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS postal_code_count,
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified_buildings_postal,
    AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_percent_covered_postal,
    AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_percent_qualified_postal,
    SUM(number_of_panels_total) AS total_panels_postal,
    SUM(kw_total) AS total_kw_postal,
    SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total) AS total_yearly_sunlight_kwh_postal,
    SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons) AS total_carbon_offset_postal,
    SUM(existing_installs_count) AS total_existing_installs_postal,
    -- Sum count_qualified directly as it represents buildings suitable for solar
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified_postal
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`
  GROUP BY state_name
),

-- Combine both aggregation levels for comparison
combined AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(t.state_name, p.state_name) AS state_name,
    -- Census Tract Level Statistics
    t.total_qualified_buildings_tract AS tract_total_qualified_buildings,
    ROUND(t.avg_percent_covered_tract, 4) AS tract_avg_percent_covered,
    ROUND(t.avg_percent_qualified_tract, 4) AS tract_avg_percent_qualified,
    t.total_panels_tract AS tract_total_panels,
    ROUND(t.total_kw_tract, 4) AS tract_total_kw,
    ROUND(t.total_yearly_sunlight_kwh_tract, 4) AS tract_total_yearly_sunlight_kwh,
    ROUND(t.total_carbon_offset_tract, 4) AS tract_total_carbon_offset,
    t.total_existing_installs_tract AS tract_existing_installs,
    -- Gap calculation for tract level:
    -- Adjusted qualified buildings = total qualified buildings (already covered and suitable)
    -- The question asks to adjust total qualified buildings with coverage and suitability percentages.
    -- Since count_qualified already includes the filtering of both percent_covered and percent_qualified,
    -- we need to compute from the raw building counts. However, raw building counts are not available.
    -- Instead, we interpret the question as: 
    -- Total buildings available = tract_total_qualified_buildings / (avg_percent_covered * avg_percent_qualified)
    -- This gives an estimate of total buildings that could potentially be considered.
    -- Then adjusted qualified = total_buildings * avg_percent_covered * avg_percent_qualified = tract_total_qualified_buildings
    -- So the gap = tract_total_qualified_buildings - existing_installs
    -- This interpretation makes count_qualified as the final qualified count.
    (t.total_qualified_buildings_tract - t.total_existing_installs_tract) AS tract_installation_gap,
    
    -- Postal Code Level Statistics
    p.total_qualified_buildings_postal AS postal_total_qualified_buildings,
    ROUND(p.avg_percent_covered_postal, 4) AS postal_avg_percent_covered,
    ROUND(p.avg_percent_qualified_postal, 4) AS postal_avg_percent_qualified,
    p.total_panels_postal AS postal_total_panels,
    ROUND(p.total_kw_postal, 4) AS postal_total_kw,
    ROUND(p.total_yearly_sunlight_kwh_postal, 4) AS postal_total_yearly_sunlight_kwh,
    ROUND(p.total_carbon_offset_postal, 4) AS postal_total_carbon_offset,
    p.total_existing_installs_postal AS postal_existing_installs,
    (p.total_qualified_buildings_postal - p.total_existing_installs_postal) AS postal_installation_gap
  FROM tract_stats t
  FULL OUTER JOIN postal_stats p
    ON t.state_name = p.state_name
)

-- Final selection with all requested metrics
SELECT 
  state_name,
  -- Census Tract Metrics
  tract_total_qualified_buildings AS tract_buildings_available,
  tract_avg_percent_covered AS tract_avg_coverage_pct,
  tract_avg_percent_qualified AS tract_avg_suitability_pct,
  tract_total_panels AS tract_total_panel_count,
  tract_total_kw AS tract_total_kw_capacity,
  tract_total_yearly_sunlight_kwh AS tract_energy_gen_kwh,
  tract_total_carbon_offset AS tract_carbon_offset_tons,
  tract_existing_installs AS tract_current_solar_installs,
  tract_installation_gap AS tract_installation_gap,
  
  -- Postal Code Metrics
  postal_total_qualified_buildings AS postal_buildings_available,
  postal_avg_percent_covered AS postal_avg_coverage_pct,
  postal_avg_percent_qualified AS postal_avg_suitability_pct,
  postal_total_panels AS postal_total_panel_count,
  postal_total_kw AS postal_total_kw_capacity,
  postal_total_yearly_sunlight_kwh AS postal_energy_gen_kwh,
  postal_total_carbon_offset AS postal_carbon_offset_tons,
  postal_existing_installs AS postal_current_solar_installs,
  postal_installation_gap AS postal_installation_gap
FROM combined
ORDER BY state_name;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Aggregate solar potential data at the state level from postal code regions
postal_agg AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    -- Derive total buildings in Google Maps: count_qualified represents buildings that are
    -- both covered AND suitable. So total = count_qualified / (pct_qualified) / (pct_covered)
    SUM(count_qualified / NULLIF(percent_qualified / 100, 0) / NULLIF(percent_covered / 100, 0)) 
      AS total_buildings,
    AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_percent_covered,
    AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_percent_qualified,
    SUM(number_of_panels_total) AS total_panel_count,
    SUM(kw_total) AS total_kw_capacity,
    SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total) AS total_energy_kwh,
    SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons) AS total_carbon_offset_tons,
    SUM(existing_installs_count) AS total_existing_installs,
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`
  WHERE percent_covered > 0 AND percent_qualified > 0
  GROUP BY state_name
),

-- Aggregate solar potential data at the state level from census tract regions
census_agg AS (
  SELECT
    state_name,
    SUM(count_qualified / NULLIF(percent_qualified / 100, 0) / NULLIF(percent_covered / 100, 0)) 
      AS total_buildings,
    AVG(percent_covered) AS avg_percent_covered,
    AVG(percent_qualified) AS avg_percent_qualified,
    SUM(number_of_panels_total) AS total_panel_count,
    SUM(kw_total) AS total_kw_capacity,
    SUM(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total) AS total_energy_kwh,
    SUM(carbon_offset_metric_tons) AS total_carbon_offset_tons,
    SUM(existing_installs_count) AS total_existing_installs,
    SUM(count_qualified) AS total_qualified
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
  WHERE percent_covered > 0 AND percent_qualified > 0
  GROUP BY state_name
)

-- Compare postal code vs census tract metrics side-by-side per state
SELECT
  COALESCE(p.state_name, c.state_name) AS state,

  -- ===== Postal Code Level Metrics =====
  ROUND(p.total_buildings, 4)          AS pc_total_buildings,
  ROUND(p.avg_percent_covered, 4)      AS pc_avg_pct_covered,
  ROUND(p.avg_percent_qualified, 4)    AS pc_avg_pct_qualified,
  p.total_panel_count                  AS pc_total_panels,
  ROUND(p.total_kw_capacity, 4)        AS pc_total_kw_capacity,
  ROUND(p.total_energy_kwh, 4)         AS pc_energy_kwh,
  ROUND(p.total_carbon_offset_tons, 4) AS pc_co2_offset_tons,
  p.total_existing_installs            AS pc_existing_installs,
  -- Gap = total qualified (suitable) buildings minus current installations
  p.total_qualified - p.total_existing_installs AS pc_potential_gap,

  -- ===== Census Tract Level Metrics =====
  ROUND(c.total_buildings, 4)          AS ct_total_buildings,
  ROUND(c.avg_percent_covered, 4)      AS ct_avg_pct_covered,
  ROUND(c.avg_percent_qualified, 4)    AS ct_avg_pct_qualified,
  c.total_panel_count                  AS ct_total_panels,
  ROUND(c.total_kw_capacity, 4)        AS ct_total_kw_capacity,
  ROUND(c.total_energy_kwh, 4)         AS ct_energy_kwh,
  ROUND(c.total_carbon_offset_tons, 4) AS ct_co2_offset_tons,
  c.total_existing_installs            AS ct_existing_installs,
  c.total_qualified - c.total_existing_installs AS ct_potential_gap

FROM postal_agg p
FULL OUTER JOIN census_agg c 
  ON p.state_name = c.state_name
ORDER BY state;
```
</details>

```sql
),

-- Step 2: Count distraction-related accidents per state for 2015 and 2016
-- Join with accident tables to get state_name
distraction_counts_2015 AS (
  SELECT
    a.state_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d.consecutive_number) AS accident_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.distract_2015` d
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_2015` a
    ON d.consecutive_number = a.consecutive_number

),

distraction_counts_2016 AS (
  SELECT
    a.state_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d.consecutive_number) AS accident_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.distract_2016` d
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_2016` a
    ON d.consecutive_number = a.consecutive_number
  WHERE d.driver_distracted_by_name NOT IN ('Not Distracted', 'Unknown if Distracted', 'Not Reported')
  GROUP BY a.state_name
),

-- Step 3: Combine counts with population, compute rate per 100k
rates_2015 AS (
  SELECT
    2015 AS year,
    sp.state_name,
    COALESCE(d.accident_count, 0) AS accident_count,
    sp.population,
    ROUND(100000.0 * COALESCE(d.accident_count, 0) / sp.population, 4) AS rate_per_100k
  FROM state_population sp
  LEFT JOIN distraction_counts_2015 d ON sp.state_name = d.state_name
),

rates_2016 AS (
  SELECT
    2016 AS year,
    sp.state_name,
    COALESCE(d.accident_count, 0) AS accident_count,
    sp.population,
    ROUND(100000.0 * COALESCE(d.accident_count, 0) / sp.population, 4) AS rate_per_100k
  FROM state_population sp
  LEFT JOIN distraction_counts_2016 d ON sp.state_name = d.state_name
),

-- Step 4: Combine both years and rank
combined AS (
  SELECT * FROM rates_2015
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM rates_2016
),

ranked AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    state_name,
    rate_per_100k,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY rate_per_100k DESC) AS rank
  FROM combined
)

-- Step 5: Final output: top 5 states per year
SELECT
  year,
  state_name,
  rate_per_100k,
  rank
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY year, rank;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Extract state code from consecutive_number and count distracted crashes for 2015
  distracted_2015 AS (
    SELECT
      SUBSTR(SAFE_CAST(d.consecutive_number AS STRING), 1, 2) AS state_code,
      COUNT(DISTINCT d.consecutive_number) AS crash_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.distract_2015` d
    WHERE LOWER(d.driver_distracted_by_name) NOT IN (
      'not distracted', 'unknown if distracted', 'not reported'
    )
    GROUP BY state_code
  ),

  -- Same for 2016
  distracted_2016 AS (
    SELECT
      SUBSTR(SAFE_CAST(d.consecutive_number AS STRING), 1, 2) AS state_code,
      COUNT(DISTINCT d.consecutive_number) AS crash_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.distract_2016` d
    WHERE LOWER(d.driver_distracted_by_name) NOT IN (
      'not distracted', 'unknown if distracted', 'not reported'
    )
    GROUP BY state_code
  ),

  -- Map state_code to state_name (using us_states_area)
  state_mapping AS (
    SELECT
      state_geo_id AS state_code,
      state_name
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.us_states_area`
    WHERE state_name IS NOT NULL AND state_name != ''
  ),

  -- Combine to get crash counts per state name
  crashes_per_state_2015 AS (
    SELECT
      m.state_name,
      d.crash_count
    FROM distracted_2015 d
    JOIN state_mapping m ON d.state_code = m.state_code
  ),

  crashes_per_state_2016 AS (
    SELECT
      m.state_name,
      d.crash_count
    FROM distracted_2016 d
    JOIN state_mapping m ON d.state_code = m.state_code
  ),

  -- Get state-level population from 2010 census (using zipcode-area mapping)
  state_population AS (
    SELECT
      z.state_name,
      SUM(SAFE_CAST(p.population AS INT64)) AS total_population
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_2010` p
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area` z
      ON p.zipcode = z.zipcode
    WHERE z.state_name IS NOT NULL
      AND z.state_name != ''
    GROUP BY z.state_name
  ),

  -- Calculate rate per 100k for 2015
  rates_2015 AS (
    SELECT
      c.state_name,
      c.crash_count,
      sp.total_population,
      ROUND((c.crash_count * 100000.0) / NULLIF(sp.total_population, 0), 2) AS rate_per_100k,
      '2015' AS year
    FROM crashes_per_state_2015 c
    JOIN state_population sp ON c.state_name = sp.state_name
  ),

  -- Calculate rate per 100k for 2016
  rates_2016 AS (
    SELECT
      c.state_name,
      c.crash_count,
      sp.total_population,
      ROUND((c.crash_count * 100000.0) / NULLIF(sp.total_population, 0), 2) AS rate_per_100k,
      '2016' AS year
    FROM crashes_per_state_2016 c
    JOIN state_population sp ON c.state_name = sp.state_name
  ),

  -- Combine both years and rank
  all_rates AS (
    SELECT * FROM rates_2015
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM rates_2016
  ),

  ranked AS (
    SELECT
      state_name,
      year,
      rate_per_100k,
      DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY rate_per_100k DESC) AS rank
    FROM all_rates
  )

-- Select top 5 states per year
SELECT
  state_name,
  year,
  rate_per_100k
FROM ranked
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY year, rank;
```
</details>

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| state_name           |   accident_difference |
|:---------------------|----------------------:|
| Virginia             |                    18 |
| Alaska               |                    -6 |
| District of Columbia |                    -7 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Understand the question: 
-- We need the top 3 states with the largest difference in number of traffic accidents 
-- between rainy and clear weather during weekends in 2016.
-- Difference = (rainy accident count) - (clear accident count) for each state.
-- Since the dataset contains only fatal accidents, we assume "traffic accidents" refer to fatal crashes.

-- Step 2: Identify relevant tables and columns:
-- Main table: bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_2016
-- Columns needed:
--   - state_name (for state identification)
--   - atmospheric_conditions_1_name (or atmospheric_conditions_name) for weather condition
--   - day_of_week (1=Sunday, 2=Monday, ..., 7=Saturday) to identify weekends (Saturday=7, Sunday=1)

-- Step 3: Define weather conditions:
-- Clear: atmospheric_conditions_1_name = 'Clear'
-- Rainy: We need to identify rain conditions. Looking at the code descriptions,
-- typical rain-related codes include 'Rain' (code 2) and possibly other variations.
-- From sample data, 'Rain' appears in atmospheric_conditions_1_name and atmospheric_conditions_name.
-- We'll use atmospheric_conditions_1_name as primary weather indicator.

-- Step 4: Build the query structure using CTEs:
-- 1. Filter accidents in 2016 on weekends (day_of_week IN (1,7))
-- 2. Separate into clear and rainy weather groups
-- 3. Count accidents per state for each weather condition
-- 4. Join the two counts and compute the difference
-- 5. Rank by difference descending and get top 3

WITH weekend_accidents AS (
  -- Select relevant columns from 2016 accident table
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    atmospheric_conditions_1_name,
    day_of_week
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_2016`
  -- Filter for weekends: day_of_week 1 = Sunday, 7 = Saturday
  WHERE day_of_week IN (1, 7)
),

clear_weekend AS (
  -- Count clear weather accidents per state on weekends
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS clear_count
  FROM weekend_accidents
  -- 'Clear' as atmospheric condition
  WHERE LOWER(atmospheric_conditions_1_name) = 'clear'
  GROUP BY state_name
),

rainy_weekend AS (
  -- Count rainy weather accidents per state on weekends
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    COUNT(*) AS rainy_count
  FROM weekend_accidents
  -- Identify rain conditions: check for 'Rain' in the condition name
  WHERE LOWER(atmospheric_conditions_1_name) LIKE '%rain%'
  GROUP BY state_name
),

differences AS (
  -- Join the two counts and compute difference (rainy - clear)
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(r.state_name, c.state_name) AS state_name,
    COALESCE(r.rainy_count, 0) AS rainy_count,
    COALESCE(c.clear_count, 0) AS clear_count,
    (COALESCE(r.rainy_count, 0) - COALESCE(c.clear_count, 0)) AS accident_difference
  FROM rainy_weekend r
  FULL OUTER JOIN clear_weekend c
    ON r.state_name = c.state_name
),

ranked_differences AS (
  -- Rank states by accident_difference descending
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    accident_difference,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY accident_difference DESC) AS rn
  FROM differences
)

-- Final output: top 3 states with largest differences
SELECT 
  state_name,
  accident_difference
FROM ranked_differences
WHERE rn <= 3
ORDER BY accident_difference DESC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH weekend_accidents AS (
  SELECT 
    state_name,
    CASE 
      WHEN atmospheric_conditions_1_name = 'Rain' THEN 'Rainy'
      WHEN atmospheric_conditions_1_name = 'Clear' THEN 'Clear'
    END AS weather_type
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_2016`
  WHERE 
    EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM timestamp_of_crash) IN (1, 7)   -- Sunday=1, Saturday=7
    AND atmospheric_conditions_1_name IN ('Rain', 'Clear')
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp_of_crash) = 2016       -- explicit year filter
)
SELECT 
  state_name,
  COUNTIF(weather_type = 'Rainy') - COUNTIF(weather_type = 'Clear') AS difference
FROM weekend_accidents
WHERE weather_type IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY state_name
ORDER BY difference DESC
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

<details>

```sql
-- Find the U.S. state with highest total annual revenue in billions during fiscal year 2016
-- Only considering companies with 4 quarters of data and specific revenue measure tags
WITH revenue_data AS (
    SELECT 
        s.stprba AS state,
        n.value AS revenue_value
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.submission` s
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.numbers` n
        ON s.submission_number = n.submission_number
    WHERE s.fiscal_year = 2016
        AND n.measure_tag IN ('Revenues', 'SalesRevenueNet', 'SalesRevenueGoodsNet')
        AND n.number_of_quarters = 4
        AND s.stprba IS NOT NULL 
        AND s.stprba != ''
        AND s.stprba != 'None'
)
SELECT 
    state,
    ROUND(SUM(revenue_value) / 1000000000.0, 4) AS total_revenue_billions
FROM revenue_data
GROUP BY state
ORDER BY total_revenue_billions DESC
LIMIT 1
```

```sql
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.submission`
  WHERE fiscal_year = 2016
    AND countryba = 'US'
    AND stprba IS NOT NULL 
    AND stprba != ''
),
revenue_data AS (
  SELECT 
    fs.stprba AS state_code,
    num.value AS revenue_value
  FROM filtered_submissions fs
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.numbers` num
    ON fs.submission_number = num.submission_number
  WHERE 
    num.measure_tag IN ('Revenues', 'SalesRevenueNet', 'SalesRevenueGoodsNet')
    AND num.number_of_quarters = 4
)
SELECT 
  state_code AS state,
  ROUND(SUM(revenue_value) / 1000000000.0, 2) AS total_revenue_billions
FROM revenue_data
GROUP BY state_code
ORDER BY total_revenue_billions DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
